# The Seventh Gate

Therefore take heed, and listen to me diligently:
The **Nourishment** <note>original: "Speiſung"; in alchemy, this refers to 'Cibation,' the process of adding liquid to the dry matter to sustain its growth</note> is called the feeding of our
dry **Matter**;
This is done with milk and food, both given in moderation,
Until it is brought into the third order.

->2.<-

But never give it so much that you suffocate it;
Prevent the **Dropsy** <note>an old medical term for swelling caused by excess fluid; here it refers to over-hydrating the alchemical substance</note> and **Noah’s Flood**,
Therefore give only a little, and then a little more
Of food and drink, as much as you see will be useful to it,
So that the watery **humors** <note>bodily fluids or elemental liquids</note> do not overcome the **Blood**;
Therefore let the drink be so measured
That the natural appetite is not extinguished by it.

->3.<-

For if it drinks too much, one must induce vomiting,
Otherwise it will remain sick for far too long;
Therefore preserve the belly from the dropsy
And from the rupture, otherwise things will not go well.
Rather, let it suffer thirst at times
Than to pour in too much drink at once,
And prescribe its **Diet** <note>a regulated regimen of heat and moisture</note> while it is in its youth.

->4.<-

Therefore it shall follow a diet as nature requires,
Which should be moderate until it reaches its full age;
Keep it in the warmth, and protect it from cold and
->moisture,<-
Then its **Power** <note>original: "Krafft"; the potency or transformative energy of the stone</note> will grow and be increased.

# The Tenth Gate: Concerning Exaltation

->1.<-

Let us now take up the chapter concerning Exaltation <note>Latin: *Exaltatio*; a process where the dignity and power of a substance is raised, often through repeated refinement</note>,
Of which you must have a complete understanding,
For it does not differ much from sublimation <note>The process of turning a solid into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note>,
Provided you have correctly understood our words;
And Holy Scripture agrees with this,
Where Christ speaks: "When I am exalted <note>original: "erhöhet"; referring to John 12:32, "And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me."</note>,
I will draw all things to myself."

->2.<-

When you exalt our Medicine <note>The "Philosopher's Stone" or the transformative substance in its developing state</note> in such a manner,
It will be ennobled in this way,
Which must happen in two ways:
From the time that the parts are married together,
Which are crucified and deprived of soul;
There, husband and wife are buried,
And are afterwards made alive again through the spirit of life.

->3.<-

Then they must be exalted up into heaven,
So that body and soul may be glorified there;
For you must bring it to such subtlety
That they can ascend together and be enthroned
In shining clouds in the company of angels;
Then they will draw, as you shall see,
All bodies to their own dignity.

# Warning Treatise.

As one who has <term>experimented<note>original: "experimentiret"; refers to the practical, hands-on testing of chemical procedures</note></term> very much in all sorts of matters,

Beginning with the work of <term>cinnabar<note>original: "Zinobers"; a bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide, often used as a starting material for quicksilver</note></term>, which was worth nothing,
And with sublimated <term>mercury<note>original: "Mercurio"; quicksilver that has been purified through heating into vapor and back to solid</note></term>, which cost me dearly.

->2.<-

Many <term>sublimations<note>The process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then condenses back into a solid form, used for purification</note></term> I have performed on the spirits,
The <term>ferments<note>Substances believed to act like yeast, "leavening" the alchemical material to transform it</note></term>, <term>salts<note>original: "salien"; various mineral salts used in chemical reactions</note></term>, iron, and steel,

# George Ripley’s Little Book
## on the Mercury of the Sages
### and their Stone.

Beloved son, I wish to instruct you in this blessed science, which was kept hidden by the ancient Sages, to whom God wished to show this great grace because of their good works and godliness, as well as because of their diligent prayers offered to God. In His name, we begin to reveal this secret to you. Note, therefore, that our Matter <note>The "Matter" refers to the *materia prima* or the raw starting material required to begin the alchemical process.</note> is the highest of all things found in the earth, yet it is the least honored or valued, as you will hear more clearly hereafter. For when the Water incorporates itself with the Earth, it is the lowliest of all things; and unless it is fixed <note>original: *figiret*. In alchemy, "fixation" is the process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat.</note> through the fire, it rises into the heights. In such a way, you can see how the Water is both the highest and the lowest.

That which I said before—that it is the least valued—is true; for in our Earth is Water, and you will find pure and clear water in the ugly earth, which is our <term>seed</term> <note>original: *sperma*. Alchemists often used biological terms to describe the "generative" power of their minerals.</note> and <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence," or the purest, most concentrated medicinal core of a substance.</note>. That same ugly earth, however, is then worth nothing more and is esteemed as nothing. But that which I said—that the Water is the highest—can be demonstrated in many ways, just as my son will know that we can make no bread without water, nor anything else that God has created in the world. From this, you can easily conclude that Water is the first matter <note>original: *erste Materi*. Also known as the *prima materia*, the formless base of all physical reality in alchemical theory.</note> of all things in the

# On the Mercury of the Sages. #

...would <note>Completing the catchword from the previous page: "would be as we..."</note> have mentioned at the beginning. Physical <term>fermentation</term> increases the weight and the <term>quantity</term> of the <term>medicine [Medicin: the transformative substance before it is finalized]</term>, yet it is not of such great power as the <term>medicine</term> itself, or as the spiritual <term>fermentation</term> is; for it only increases the <term>medicine</term> in <term>quantity</term>, but not in virtue. Moreover, as long as the <term>medicine</term> is <term>fermented</term> with spiritual <term>qualities</term>, it is called <term>medicine</term>; but when it is <term>fermented</term> with a <term>physical [corporalisch]</term> substance, it is called an <term>elixir [Elixir: a more fixed, dense form of the medicine used for transmutation]</term>. Let him who has understanding understand it, for it is not permitted to say more; and provided you understand this, I do not doubt that you will never make these great secrets common knowledge.

# The Marrow of Chemical Philosophy by George Ripley,
<note>original: "Medulla Philosophiæ Chemicæ Georgii Riplæi"</note>

## The Author’s Preface to an English Canon.

Since I have undertaken to treat the secrets of the chemical art, I shall make it my concern to reveal to Your Reverence that which I have experienced and learned through much labor for nine whole years in Italy and the neighboring lands. In this work, I intend to extract, as it were, the marrow and core of nature—which I have already tested through experiment—and separate it from the inner, hidden bones and dregs of the substance. 

All of this I wish to explain to you clearly and briefly in this writing of mine (to which my singular love for you compels me); I shall speak plainly and without reservation, truthfully and not obscurely, quite clearly and not hidden. For the life you lead is testified to by your good works, as you are a refuge for the Christian flock, a light of the Catholic Church, and a pillar of our faith. 

And to whom else should I make such a secret known but to you? For this knowledge can make you more joyful of heart, more devout of spirit, healthier of body, richer in good deeds, more pleasant in merits, more generous in giving, more diligent in being of use to all, and even more beneficial to the Church—as you are such a renowned Bishop, a

# Marrow of the Art.

Now, to proceed to the first point of this my undertaking, I have found it written that once a great company of philosophers gathered together, among whom a question arose concerning their <term>secret stone</term> <note>original: *geheimen Stein*. The Philosopher’s Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and silver.</note> and the order of its <term>administration</term> <note>original: *Administration*. The practical management and sequence of operations in the laboratory.</note>. Now, as many of them brought forth their <term>reasons</term> <note>original: *rationes*. Logical arguments or theoretical proofs.</note> to explain this question, finally one among them, who was not as old and learned as the others, was asked what his opinion was and what he thought he knew of this matter. He answered that he knew the <term>governments of the fire</term> <note>original: *Regirungen des Feuers*. In alchemy, the "regimen" refers to the precise control of heat levels—ranging from gentle digestion to intense smelting—required at different stages of the work.</note>. When the others heard this, they were all gradually struck with awe; and one among them answered in this way: "If it is as you say, then you are truly master over us all." And so they granted him the honor, as he seemed worthy of it.

What else can we conclude from these words but that a great part of our secret lies in the fire? But such fire differs in various ways; for there is a **Natural** fire, another is **Unnatural**, another is **Elemental**, and another is the **Fire against Nature**.

**Natural fire** is that which comes from the <term>influence</term> <note>original: *influenz*. The 17th-century belief that celestial bodies emitted an ethereal power or "fluid" that shaped life and minerals on Earth.</note> of the sun, the moon, and the stars, from which are generated the <term>spirits</term> <note>original: *spiritus*. Volatile substances or the vital essence contained within matter.</note> of the <term>burning waters</term> <note>original: *brennenden Wasser*. Usually refers to distilled alcohols or strong mineral acids used as solvents.</note>, the essential vapors of the minerals, as well as the natural powers of all living things.

**Unnatural fire** is that which arises by occasion, such as the heat in fevers; it is called by the philosophers the **moist fire**, which is made by art. It is also called the **fire of the first degree**, which

However, this very same oil, when placed in a sealed chemical vessel and kept in the heat of the first degree or <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "putrefaction"; the stage of decomposition or rotting, often called the "Nigredo" or blackening</note>, becomes as black as liquid pitch; and this is the <term>prime matter</term> <note>original: "prima materia"; the raw, formless base substance required for the alchemical Great Work</note> of **mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii"</note> and **sulfur** <note>original: "sulphuris"</note>, for then the fire can demonstrate its <term>action</term> <note>original: "action"</note> upon a body thus opened and made ready for <term>corruption</term> <note>original: "corruption"; the breakdown of a substance's current form so it can be reborn in a higher state</note>. Since, without such a **dissolving solvent** <note>original: *menstruum resolutivum*</note>, no dissolution can ever occur. 

Such a resolving solvent arises solely from the genus of metals; for there is a **potential vapor** <note>original: *vapor potentialis*; a latent gas or essence within the metal</note> in every metallic body. This is that which **conjoins** <note>original: *conjungirt*; binds together</note> the two **extremes** <note>original: *extrema*</note>, namely sulfur and mercury. Thus, our water is a metallic water, and because it retains the nature of those two extremes, it is brought **into action** <note>original: *in actum*; from a state of potential to a state of active power</note> through our resolving solvent. 

But as to how such a solvent is to be obtained—one that is unctuous <note>oily or fatty</note>, moist, sulfurous, and mercurial, and which agrees well with the nature of metals, and with which our body must be **dissolved** <note>original: *dissolviret*</note> through art—this we wish to show here with clear **practice** <note>original: *Practic*; a practical laboratory recipe</note>: Take the sharpest moisture of the grapes, which has been distilled, and **dissolve** <note>original: *solvire*</note> therein that body which has been well calcined <note>reduced to a powder through high heat</note> until it reached a red color—which the philosophers call **fricon** <note>a technical term in Lullian alchemy for a specifically prepared metallic substance or 'body'</note>—into a clear crystalline...

## The Third Chapter.

### In what manner the errors / which arise from the interpretation of obscure words / are to be avoided.

Since we have compassion for the ignorance of the students / whose necks have not yet been softened by the alchemical <term>ointment</term> <note>original: *ung- ent* (Unguent). This is a metaphorical way of saying the students have not yet been "anointed" or initiated into the smooth flow of alchemical wisdom.</note> / and we have previously made the promise / that we would communicate different manners of practice in this Art; Therefore, to explain the truth in the simplest way / I will clearly deal with the meaning of several obscure words / and clarify them. Thus, it is to be noted / that the philosophers place many and various names in their books / so that they may not be understood by fools / and the science fall into contempt / and also not become common to all without distinction / to the worthy and the wicked alike; 

But the philosophers have not concerned themselves with the names / but with the truth of the names; For our <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the elusive goal of alchemy believed to enable the transmutation of metals and the healing of the human body.</note> may be called whatever it may be / yet it is still only a single thing / which / if it were known / would not be allowed to be common / as it is to the poor and the rich; it would also not lie in the streets / and be trodden underfoot by men; And so that I may reveal this thing / know by God / that such a thing is one of those / which are named after the <term>seven days</term> <note>In alchemy, the "seven days" refers to the seven celestial bodies and their corresponding metals: the Sun (Gold), the Moon (Silver), Mars (Iron), Mercury (Quicksilver), Jupiter (Tin), Venus (Copper), and Saturn (Lead).</note> / and among those it is the lowly <note>The text cuts off here at "the lowly," which likely refers to Saturn (lead) or another metal considered "base" or common.</note>

Therefore, take mercury that has been washed with salt and vinegar, and incorporate one part of it with four pounds of Roman vitriol <term>Roman Vitriol: historically, this usually refers to blue vitriol (copper sulfate) or green vitriol (iron sulfate)</term> and with four ounces of well-burnt common salt. # George Ripley's Treatise / Called the Key of the Golden Gates.

Since it has been found in what manner the path of truth to attaining mastery in the chemical art was closed / I, George Ripley <note>George Ripley (c. 1415–1490) was a famous English alchemist and canon of Bridlington whose works were foundational to later European alchemy</note>, have resolved to gather here into a brief summary that which is contained in the science of **Alchemy** across many and various books and writings of the **Philosophers** <note>In this context, "Philosophers" refers to alchemical authorities and natural scientists of antiquity</note> who have written on this subject; namely from the books of **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many foundational alchemical texts are attributed</note>, **Morienus**, **Calid** <note>referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an Umayyad prince credited with early alchemical interests</note>, the ***Turba Philosophorum*** <note>original: *Turbæ Philosophorum*; one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts, written as a transcript of a meeting of ancient philosophers</note>, and others of the like; If we consider the entire philosophical intention / namely, that all metals are generated from **Mercury** and **Sulphur** <note>original: *Mercurio und sulphur*; alchemists believed all metals were composed of these two "principles" (philosophical mercury and sulfur) in different proportions and purities</note> / and from that which they consist / from that must their **Medicine** <note>In alchemy, the "Medicine" refers to the Elixir or Philosopher's Stone, which was thought to "cure" base metals of their impurities to turn them into gold</note> also be made; Thus, we must take quicksilver and sulfur as the material for our **Stone**; Just as metals are not generated from quicksilver alone, nor from sulfur alone, but from the mixing of them both / it is therefore evident / that our material must also be taken from them. However, the practitioner of this science must be endowed with a subtle understanding / and must well know and recognize the nature of metals / and their innumerable births within their ore-veins. And it is therefore fitting to pay attention to the natures of things / which do not appear visibly / but remain according to their **potential** <note>original: *potentialiter*; the hidden power or capacity within a substance to be transformed into something else</note>.

# § 584 Key of the Golden Gates.

for water is a cold and moist element, but fire is a hot and dry element; therefore, water must first be made into air, which is an intermediary element between water and fire. For as soon as the coldness of water is transformed into warmth, the water is immediately changed into air; and further, the moisture of the water must be transformed into dryness, so that the water is then changed into its opposite element—that is, into fire. 

In such a manner one must also proceed if one wishes to turn fire into water in a descending fashion: namely, so that the heat of the fire is turned into the coldness of water, one must first turn the fire into earth, which is an intermediary element between fire and water when one descends from the other side. Subsequently, the dryness of the fire must be turned into moisture, and thus the fire is changed into the element of water, which is its contrary. 

Likewise, if one desires through the Art <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy, specifically the practical work of transmuting substances.</note> to transform earth into air in an ascending manner, or air into earth in a descending manner, then in descending, the earth must first become fire. Thus, through the power of the intermediary element, every element can be transformed into another; and this is certainly not found in any other author as it is here.

# Key of the Golden Gates.
588

you might rightly bear the name of a *philosopher* <note>original: "Philosophi"; here meaning a natural philosopher or alchemist</note> not unskilled in natural things; but it is to be noted that the ancient philosophers did not use common gold and silver for this work, and for that reason said that such labor does not require much expense and can be performed as well by the poor and peasants as by the rich and city-dwellers. This would in no way agree with the truth if the Art <note>The "Great Work" of alchemy</note> could not be performed without common gold and silver; for these are very expensive and rare, and do not fall to the poor without great toil. 

Indeed, many have destroyed a great quantity of gold and silver in this Art and consumed their time and labor quite uselessly, with the loss of both body and soul—which, in my opinion, is heartily to be lamented. Likewise, in this our own time, we have known almost no one who has earnestly devoted himself to the true **tinctures** <note>original: "tincturen"; the transmuting essences that change the quality of metals</note> of the philosophers, but most have troubled themselves quite absurdly and generally in vain with common **mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>, gold, and silver. For that reason, quite few have received this grace; on the contrary, we have seen very many who have quite miserably squandered all they owned. 

Therefore, let us be cautious; for although gold and silver may be refined <note>original: "subtilisiret"; the alchemical process of making a substance more subtle, pure, or volatile</note> and mixed into the tinctures, and further brought into small **elixirs** <note>original: "Elixiren"</note> and indeed with profit, yet the true way according to the **intent** <note>original: "intention"</note> of the philosophers is not to be sought in them. # Key to the Golden Portals.

...width, depth, and length. Width means as much as opening a metal, that is, preparing it for **dissolution** <note>original: "dissolution"; the process of breaking a solid down into a liquid</note> or resolution.

Depth means as much as bringing it back into a **first matter** <term>First matter: (Latin: *prima materia*) The formless primeval substance from which all things are made, sought by alchemists as the starting point for the Great Work</term> or original essence; that is, separating the volatile from the fixed, and the **tincture** <note>original: "tinctur"; a potent liquid extract or the essence that colors and transforms metals</note> from the earth. Length means as much as **extending** <note>original: "extendiren"</note> or spreading out, and **multiplying** <note>original: "multipliciren"</note> our tincture and its power to infinity. From these, three others are **derived** <note>original: "deriviret"</note> or led forth: namely, **dissolving** <note>original: "solviren"</note>, **liquefying** <note>original: "dissolviren"</note>, and **resolving** <note>original: "resolviren"</note>.

**To dissolve** <note>original: "solviren"</note> is as much as bringing a dry material back into a moist state; for through the **solution** <note>original: "solution"</note>, the **sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note> is **separated** <note>original: "separiret"</note> from the **mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>, which is to say, the moist from the dry.

**To liquefy** <note>original: "dissolviren"</note> is as much as making the coarse body subtle or thinning it, and bringing it into a finer substance.

**To resolve** <note>original: "resolviren"</note> is as much as dissolving anew that which was previously dissolved and then **coagulated** <note>original: "coaguliret"; hardened back into a solid</note> again. For example: if one lays a salt upon a stone, it dissolves into water, for it was water beforehand.

That which is dissolved continues to dissolve, which is its nature, provided that the dissolved does not exceed the dissolver; for every metal is dissolved by its own **mercury** <note>In alchemy, Mercury and Sulfur represent the fundamental philosophical principles of liquidity/volatility and combustion/solidity rather than just the common elements</note>. The **solution**, **liquefaction** <note>original: "dissolution"</note>, and **fixation** <note>original: "fixation"; the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat so it does not evaporate</note> require a warm place, but the **resolution** and **congealing** <note>original: "congelation"; the process of thickening or freezing a liquid into a solid</note> require a cold one. For if a salt is placed in a bladder and held in warm water, it **represents** <note>original: "repræsentiret"</note> the liquefaction, but not the **reso-**

# Key to the Golden Portals.

## Concerning the Colors.

Blackness is assigned to the Earth; for we know that all the other elements are contained within the Earth.

Whiteness is attributed to the Water; for Whiteness is crystalline, and Water is likewise crystalline.

Citrinity <term>Citrinität: the "yellowing" stage in alchemy, representing the transition from the white work to the final red goal</term> or Yellowness is granted to the Air: for we see at the upper part of fire some yellowness which comes from the Air.

Redness is attributed to the Fire, and therefore it is said that the angels were created from the pure element of Fire and have the power to penetrate through all things; and so too does the Philosopher’s Stone, as it consists of pure fire and has the power to fix <note>original: "figiren"; to make a volatile substance solid and heat-resistant</note>, penetrate <note>original: "penetriren"</note>, and tinge <note>original: "tingiren"; to transform the color and nature of a metal</note> all bodies; for we see that within much Redness, the yellow color is contained; in the yellow, the white; in the white, the black; and conversely, in the black, the white; in the white, the yellow; and in the yellow, the red—and thus you have the **Philosophical Wheel** <note>original: "Philosophische Rad"; a symbolic representation of the repeating cycles of the alchemical process</note>.

### End of the treatise called the Key to the Golden Portals.

# George Ripley’s Treatise
### called
## The Pupil of the Eye of Alchemy.
### Author’s Preface.

First, learn to understand what Avicenna <note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), a Persian polymath whose medical and philosophical works were foundational to medieval European alchemy</note> says: that in lead, gold and silver exist potentially <note>original: "per potentiam"; meaning they have the capacity to become these metals even if they aren't yet</note> and not by visibility; and these were left by nature as still raw and only half-boiled. Therefore, one must fulfill through the Art <note>The "Art" refers to the practice of alchemy</note> and bring to perfection that which is left imperfect by nature; and this is done through the door of a digesting ferment <term>ferment: a substance, often gold or silver, added to the alchemical mixture to "leaven" or direct the transformation of the base metal</term>, which thoroughly boils away what remains of rawness <note>original: "crudität"</note> or crudity. 

Take, therefore, perfect gold instead of the ferment; for in such a way, the fixed substance of the gold will gradually draw and transform many of the unfixed bodies <note>In alchemy, "unfixed" or volatile bodies are those that vaporize or change easily under heat, like lead or mercury</note> to the perfection of gold and silver. In this manner, Art will come to the aid of nature, so that in a short time, that which happens above the earth can accomplish what would otherwise take nearly a thousand years to occur beneath the earth <note>Alchemists believed that metals "grew" in the earth like plants, slowly maturing from base metals into gold over vast spans of geological time</note>. 

And in this sense, you will understand in what manner lead contains within itself the highest secrets of this Art. For it has within itself a pure, clear, and fragrant mercury <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note> which has not yet been brought to perfection by nature; and this

## Another Way.

So that we may now also speak of the other method; Raymond Lully <note>original: *Raimundus*; a 13th-century philosopher and supposed alchemist</note> wrote to King Robert in his *Shortened Letter* <note>original: *epist. accurtat.* or *Epistola Accurtatoria*</note> in this manner: 

Dissolve red **calx of gold** <note>gold that has been chemically reduced to a powder or "ash"</note> and, at the same time, the previously mentioned **Mercury** in a very strong corrosive water <note>an acid, likely aqua regia</note> made from **vitriol** <term>sulfate minerals</term> and **saltpeter** <term>potassium nitrate</term>, as is the common custom. And when they are dissolved together, put them into a circulation glass <note>a specialized flask used for constant evaporation and condensation</note>, and place it in the water bath <note>original: *Balneum*</note> in an open vessel until half of the water has evaporated and the material at the bottom of the vessel becomes thick. 

Then seal the circulation glass with a strong **lute** <note>original: *luto*; a paste or clay used to seal alchemical vessels airtight</note>, and let the remaining part of the corrosive acid fix itself <note>original: *figiren*; to turn a volatile substance into a stable, solid form</note> into a dry powder in mild ash-heat. Repeat this work—dissolving, evaporating, and fixing—about ten times. 

You will then have an oily material which will no longer take in any more of the corrosive water, nor will it subsequently allow itself to be fixed into a powder, but will remain in the form of a thick oil. This oil fixes **Mercury** and other metallic bodies into the most perfect gold; and such gold is suitable for all goldsmith's work, but not for human bodies <note>this chemical gold was considered "dead" or toxic compared to "potable gold" intended for medicine</note>. Concerning the **multiplication** <note>the process of increasing the potency or quantity of the alchemical agent</note> of this substance, see Lully in his *Magic* <note>original: *magia*</note>. Cast this thick oil onto ten parts of purified **Mercury**, and it will turn into a powder.

As for what further concerns this work, I know of no truer works than these which I have explained here. Therefore, let this satisfy you, to the praise and honor of God, to whom be honor and glory for all eternity, Amen.

*With two gums, fix the volatile in the depths.* <note>original Latin: *Gummis cum binis fugitivum figito in imis.* In alchemy, "gums" often refer to sticky, resinous substances or specific chemical intermediates used to "bind" volatile spirits.</note>

->That is:<-

**With two gums you shall fix the volatile substance,**
**So that it no longer rises from the bottom by sublimation.** <note>sublimation: the process where a solid turns into a gas when heated; here, the goal is to prevent the substance from "fleeing" the heat.</note>

And for this reason, no one should be surprised that a person might be able to extract our Stone <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> from plants <term>vegetabilien: organic matter</term>, animals <term>animalien: biological matter</term>, and intermediate minerals <term>Mittel-Mineralien: substances like vitriols or salts that share properties of both stones and metals</term>; for the Philosopher <note>likely referring to a classic authority like Geber or Hermes Trismegistus</note> says that those who believe the Philosopher’s Stone is made [directly] from wine, blood, eggs, and the like have conceived a false imagination and thought. However, he subsequently adds that it is possible and true to understand this when it occurs from the elements; for the elements, when they are gloriously obtained in their highest rectification <term>rectification: the process of purifying a substance through repeated distillation or refinement</term>, mix themselves with the Ferment <term>ferment: a substance, often gold or silver, added to the alchemical "medicine" to give it the specific qualities of that metal</term>, and together with it they constitute the Stone. Without this Ferment, the Stone can neither have nor give the form of gold or silver.

Therefore, one must know and note for the truth that the elements, if they are not extracted from such things, can neither enter into nor become part of the work of the Elixirs <term>Elixiren: potent medicinal or transformative substances</term>, except solely through the power and mixing with the elements that have been extracted from the metallic spirits and bodies <term>metallic spirits: volatile substances like mercury or sulfur that "animate" the dense metal bodies</term>. And the elements must be separated by their opposites <term>contraria: the alchemical theory that substances are purified by pitting opposing qualities—like heat and cold—against one another</term>; thus, the elements that are refined to the highest degree are not combustible, but either fly away entirely or remain completely. One does not need to worry about the Earth <note>in this context, "Earth" refers to the solid residue or base of the substance</note>, regarding what kind of substance it is, as long as it is fixed <term>fix: stable in fire; not evaporating or changing</term>. Fire, water, and air dry out, soak <term>imbibiren: to saturate a solid with liquid until it can hold no more</term>, and fix <term>figiren: to make a volatile substance solid or resistant to heat</term>; water and air wash away the earth and the fire, tinting and perfecting them. The third work is the feeding of the Stone through the soaking of its water. 

The fourth work is the marriage <note>the union of opposites, often the "king" and "queen" or spirit and body</note> of the Stone through the addition of its first body; and the body is the ferment <term>Ferment: an agent, like a yeast, that triggers a transformation in the whole mass</term> of the spirit. The first matter of the Stone is a sulfurous and mercurial water, and our vessel must be sealed in the Philosophical manner at the time of dissolution and governed in a moist state until the Whiteness <note>original: *Weissigkeit*. At that point, whatever is subtle and thin rises up in the vessel, but whatever is thick and coarse remains below. 

The cooking of the Stone lasts at least one hundred and fifty days. One must also have a good quantity of the non-fixed part of the water for the sake of sublimation <note>the process of heating a substance until it rises as vapor and solidifies again</note>. And one must throw away the first dregs <note>original Latin: *feces*</note>, from which this water is extracted, at the beginning of the work. Our water, which begins to effervesce when poured onto a lime <term>Kalck: a powder or oxide produced by heating a metal or mineral</term>, must be planted into another, more subtle earth. Our sulfurs can also be obtained for a small price from the materialists <note>merchants or druggists who sold raw chemical materials</note>.

# The Practice with the Tincture of Vitriol.

Calcination of Roman Vitriol <note>original: *Vitriol*; historically referring to iron or copper sulfates, essential to alchemical experiments for their acidic properties</note> over burning coals until it acquires a reddish color; then dissolve it in the <term>solvent</term> <note>original: *menstruo*; a liquid used to dissolve or extract essences, named for its cyclical or "monthly" nature in the Great Work</note>, and let it decay [putrefy] until a crystalline <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: *sulphur*; in alchemy, the "soul" or active, combustible principle of a substance</note> is formed from it; proceed with this Philosophically. In the second way, let it be dissolved according to common dissolution in the solvent which has been perfectly rectified; from this, let all moisture be distilled with a strong fire—whatever is willing to distil—which, along with the solvent, hides the tincture of Vitriol. But if one places a burning light behind the vessel and watches thus, one will see a fiery color swimming upon the solvent, so that you will praise GOD with wonder. This [tincture] you can <term>fix</term> <note>fix: to make a volatile substance solid and resistant to heat</note> upon the first or second prepared <term>calx</term> <note>original: *Kalck*; a powder or oxide remaining after a metal has been burned or calcined</note>, as it pleases you; the first is common, but the second is Philosophical. Therefore, with the help of the solvent, make the second calx from Iron, and make it red in the proper manner with the aforementioned tincture, and then dissolve it in the common way in the solvent. Also dissolve Silver in a strong <term>corrosive</term> <note>an acidic liquid, likely aqua fortis (nitric acid)</note>, and mix the solutions together; afterwards, melt it with the addition of a little fine Gold, and so everything becomes good Gold. Or make a Silver-calx, as you know how, and wax [incerate] it with the aforementioned tincture of Vitriol, which was extracted by the solvent, until it is red enough, and then melt it with half as much fine Gold. This method is easy, good, and profitable. ## The Practice with the Tincture of Vitriol.

Calcify <note>original: *Calcinire*; to heat a substance until it becomes a powder</note> Roman Vitriol <note>usually referring to iron sulfate (green vitriol) or copper sulfate (blue vitriol)</note> over burning coals / until it becomes a reddish color / then dissolve it in the menstruum <note>original: *menstruo*; a solvent used to extract the essence of a substance</note>, and let it putrefy / until a crystalline sulfur results from it / proceed philosophically with this. In the second way, let it be dissolved according to common dissolution in the menstruum / which has been perfectly rectified <note>rectified: purified through repeated distillation</note> / from which all moisture that will distill is distilled with a strong fire / which, along with the menstruum, hides the tincture of Vitriol / but if one places a burning light behind the vessel / and watches in this manner / one will see a fiery color floating upon the menstruum / so that you will praise **GOD** with wonder / you can fix <note>fix: to stabilize a volatile substance so it remains solid under heat</note> this upon the first or second prepared calx <term>calx: the powdery oxide remaining after a metal has been burned or "calcined"</term> / as it pleases you / the first is common / but the second is philosophical. Therefore, with the help of the menstruum, make the second calx from iron / and make it red in the proper measure with the aforementioned tincture / and then dissolve it in the common way in the menstruum. Also dissolve silver in a strong corrosive <note>likely an acid like nitric acid</note>, and mix the solutions together / afterward melt it with the addition of a little fine gold / and thus all becomes good gold / or make a silver-calx / as you know how / incerate <term>inceration: the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a waxy consistency</term> the same with the aforementioned tincture of Vitriol / which has been extracted through the menstruum / until it is red enough / and then melt it with half as much fine gold. This manner is easy / good / and profitable. ## An Elixir of Life <note>original: *Elixir vitæ*</note>.

Make a pelican <note>A "pelican" is a specialized alchemical flask with two side-arms that loop back into the body, designed for continuous distillation and "circulation" of a liquid.</note> one cubit high / and fill the fourth part with well-rectified vegetable menstruum <term>menstruum: a solvent, often derived from wine or vinegar, used to extract the "essence" of a substance</term>, and into the same place well-crushed spices / indeed the most precious ones / that can possibly be found. Seal the vessel hermetically <term>hermetically: airtight, usually by melting the glass neck of the vessel shut</term> / place the pelican into the water bath <note>original: *balneum*</note> in such a degree of heat / that only the vegetable spirit alone may be circulated / and continue such circulation with the same tempered degree of fire / until our wine becomes thick like an oil / so that the spirits no longer rise / in this manner you will obtain the quintessence <term>quintessence: the "fifth essence," a highly concentrated and purified spiritual form of a substance</term> / which is fixed in its heaven and is more glorious for health than all gold and silver ; This work requires a long time / for if one wishes to hurry with too strong a fire / it can never be brought to a proper conclusion.

### The powers of this quintessence can be tested in this manner.

1. Open your vessel / and you will never in this life have smelled such a lovely scent.

2. Make a circle on a table with this quintessence / place a poisonous animal into such a circle / and it will run about and die / and will never be able to crawl out over the circle.

3. It heals all illnesses and restores youth.

4. If you fix the quintessence of gold with this elixir / you will [have] the glorious drinkable gold <note>original: *aurum potabile*; a legendary medicine believed to cure all ailments</note>.

Thereafter, pour off the dissolved **liquid** <note>original: "liquorem"</note>, and filter it three times from its **dregs** <note>original: "fecibus"; the solid sediment or waste left after a substance is dissolved</note>, until it becomes as clear as a crystal. Continue with such gentle fire until you see a white smoke like milk appear in the receiver. Then place another receiver before it and strengthen the fire, sealing the receiver tightly so that no air can escape. ## Another way or form of distillation.

Prepare this by another manner or practice in this way: Take the **green lion** <term>original: "grünen Löwen"; a symbolic name for a raw mineral, often vitriol or antimony</term>, without any **dissolution** <note>original: "solution"</note> in vinegar, and put it into a large earthenware **retort** <note>a glass or ceramic vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note> that can withstand the fire. Set it to distill in the same manner as if you were brewing **parting-water** <term>Scheidwasser; nitric acid, used to separate or "part" silver from gold</term>, and place a **receiver** <note>original: "Vorlage"; the vessel that collects the distilled liquid</note> before it, diligently **sealing** <note>original: "Verlutirung"; using a paste or "lute" to make the joints airtight</note> the joints so that no air can escape.

Next, distill first with a gentle fire until you see a white smoke appear. Then put another receiver in place and seal it tightly, and distill in such a fashion with a strong fire, just as one distills **strong-water** <term>aquafort (Latin: aqua fortis); a highly corrosive mineral acid</term>. Continue this for 24 hours; and even if you should continue such a fire for a full eight days, you will constantly see the receiver full of white smoke. In this manner, you will obtain the **Blood of the Green Lion** <note>a potent, often red-colored chemical distillate</note>, which we call the **secret water**, and the sharpest vinegar through which the bodies <note>metals</note> are brought back into their **first matter** <term>primam materiam; the original, undifferentiated substance from which all materials were thought to originate</term>, and they will...

## On the Mineral Stone.

In the same way, you can proceed with the white or red, simple or mixed Mercury <note>original: *Mercurio*; in alchemy, this refers to the "principle" of fluidity and transformation rather than just common quicksilver</note> upon the sea-stones—that is, those found by the sea—just as you have behaved with the Vitriol <note>original: *Vitriol*; a sulfate mineral often used as a starting material for the "Green Lion" or acidic solvents</note>; so you will obtain a great Elixir, and through the help of our putrefaction <note>original: *putrefaction*; the stage of decay or "blackness" where matter is broken down to be reborn</note> you can alter all minerals. Therefore, the Philosophers say that an Elixir can be made from every thing that is fixed <note>original: *fix*; stable and resistant to the heat of fire</note> in the fire, since you can plant our white or red Mercury into every fixed thing—that is, if they lack Mercury—and you may transform some bodies into the form of a metal which were never a metal before. These bodies are: powdered glass and eggshell powder—which is the "earth from the mountains" that is thrown onto the dung—for when the eggshells are perfectly calcined <note>original: *calciniret*; reduced to a fine powder through intense heating</note>, they withstand the fire better than gold or silver, and no such fixed earth is found more in the world.

And such was the intention of the Philosophers: namely, to make metals above the earth in a single day, which Nature takes barely a thousand years to make beneath the earth; this seems impossible to many, and especially to the inexperienced. # The Work of the Basilisk / or the Composition of Pearls.

Take an **altered calx** <note>original: *alterirten Kalck*; a metal that has been oxidized or reduced to a powder through chemical treatment</note> and pour upon it enough of our **burning water** <note>original: *brennenden Wasser*; typically high-proof distilled alcohol or a strong mineral acid</note> so that it rises two fingers high above it, and let it stand in a **water bath** <note>original: *balneo*</note> to **dissolve** <note>original: *resolviren*</note> for five days. Then, draw up the added water through the **alembic head** <note>original: *Helm*; the top part of a still used for distillation</note>, so that a portion of the oil from the calx rises with the water; keep this. And then pour another water onto the remaining earth and **proceed** as before, and continue this until everything has been **exalted** <note>original: *exaltiret*; refined or elevated to a higher state</note> or raised into an oil together with the water. This is the **exuberant** or elevated water, as well as the **Virgin's Milk** <note>original: *Jungfern-Milch*; a traditional alchemical term for a white, milky-looking liquid or precipitate</note> and the permanent water.

The distilled waters must then be **rectified** <note>original: *rectificiren*; purified by repeated distillation</note> together until the water is entirely **crystalline**. Following each **rectification**, raise the remaining **dregs** <note>original: *feces*</note> with fresh water until everything together has been raised into a crystalline water. Put this into a vessel with a neck that is **three feet** <note>original: *drey Schuch*; literally "three shoes," an old unit of measurement approximately equal to a foot</note> high or long, and seal it well with wax. Place this vessel up to half its height in **fine earth** <note>original: *subtile Erde*; likely sand or sifted soil used for even heat distribution</note>, so that no stones touch it, and let it stand therein for an entire year. In this time, the **matter** will **congeal** <note>original: *congeliren*</note> into a transparent stone which we call the **Basilisk**. For just as the basilisk kills a human with its gaze alone, so this stone kills **common mercury** <note>original: *gemeinen Mercurium*</note> even without common fire. Thus, when it is **dissolved** <note>original: *solvirt*</note> in a water bath, it sets or **coagulates** in the cold, and dissolves or melts in the heat; and it can be made from the calx of any metal.

<summary>This page details the creation of the "Basilisk," a powerful crystalline substance made by repeatedly distilling a metal's calx until it becomes a "crystalline water" that congeals over a year. This substance is said to "kill" (stabilize) mercury instantly, even without heat.</summary>

### Of the Benedictine Order

### Fifth Part of the Last Testament

Since this is then my final book or part / and I intend to give a complete account of **potable gold** <note>original: *auro potabili*; a legendary "drinkable gold" believed to be a universal cure</note> / for the art-loving / understanding and also worthy person / whom God will gladden with this book after my end / which I myself have experienced with great, bitter toil and labor.

Therefore, if God grants you the fortune / that you attain true knowledge / see that you hold this **secret** <note>original: *arcanum*</note> in the highest secrecy / so that you do not turn God's blessing into a curse for yourself / for the preparation of the **Stone** <note>original: *Lapidis*; referring to the Philosopher's Stone</note> and **potable gold** <note>original: *auri potabilis*</note> is the same in the beginning / for they both have their origin and first birth from the true seed and astral **first mover** <note>original: *primo mobili*; the outermost sphere of the heavens that moves all others</note> / which is called the **spirit of Mercury** <note>original: *spiritus Mercurii*; in alchemy, this is the life-force or "mercurial" essence of matter, not just the liquid metal</note> / of which I have written to you extensively heretofore. For know in the highest truth / that neither **universal**- nor **particular tincture** / neither **potable gold** <note>original: *aurum potabile*</note> nor any other **Universal Medicine** <note>original: *Universal-Medicin*</note> / outside of this heavenly and spiritual essence / which takes and receives its origin from the starry sky / can be brought about / nor prepared: therefore be silent until death / then lay the talent <note>original: *Pfund*; literally "pound," a reference to the biblical Parable of the Talents regarding the duty to use and then return God-given gifts</note> down again / as I have done / for if I had not taught you faithfully / you would not know much of this mystery / but would remain sitting with the common crowd in their folly / blindness and madness / and have written a **prescription** <note>original: *Recipe*</note> into the smeared apothecary shops / where your soul would have eventually traveled / namely into the **lap of Galen** <note>original: *Schoos Galeni*; a derogatory reference to the followers of Galen, the ancient Greek physician whose traditional herbal methods were rejected by alchemists like Paracelsus</note> / into the outermost abyss of darkness / to be found in hell among all the devils in the lowest part; even so would your body and soul also be sent there / if you reveal even the smallest part.

# Now follows the Salt of Tartar.

First, you should know that the <term>Tartar</term> <note>original: "tartar" / "Weinstein"; in alchemy, this refers to the sediment found in wine barrels, but Valentine distinguishes between the common version and the "Philosophic" version.</note> of the Philosophers is not the common cream of tartar through which the lock is opened; rather, it is another salt, though they both come from the same root. It is the secret, single key to all metals, which is made as follows: From <term>vine-ashes</term> <note>original: "Reben-Aschen"; ashes from burnt grapevine wood.</note>, make a sharp <term>lye</term> <note>original: "Laugen"</note>, as sharp as is ever possible. Boil it until it is entirely dry, and a reddish <term>matter</term> <note>original: "materia"</note> will remain. <term>Reverberate</term> <note>original: "reverberir"; to heat in a furnace where the flame is reflected back onto the substance.</note> this for three hours in a flaming fire, stirring it constantly until it becomes white. Afterward, <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: "solvirs"</note> it in distilled rainwater, let the <term>dregs</term> <note>original: "feces"; the solid waste or sediment.</note> settle well, filter it, and <term>coagulate</term> <note>original: "coagulirs"; to thicken or solidify a liquid into a solid mass.</note> it until dry in a glass. Then you have the <term>Salt of Tartar</term> <note>original: "sal tartari"</note>, from which the true <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "spiritus"</note> is driven.

So that I may now come further to the description of other things, I will leave off from those just recounted, and proceed and continue to the <term>metallic salts</term> <note>original: "metallischen salien"</note> which I taught how to extract in the fourth part [of this work]. I will describe what <term>virtues</term> <note>original: "virtutes"</note>, powers, and capabilities these—alongside the following minerals and other things—possess in <term>medicine</term> <note>original: "Artzney"</note>, specifically within the human body; and first, I shall write of the **Salt of Gold**.

## Of the Salt of Copper.

The salt of copper is of a hotter nature, more so than the other <term>salts</term> <note>original: "salia"</note> of the metals; its weight for ingestion is set at only three grains at the most. It serves for the indigestion of a bad stomach, for it sets it right again, dispels <term>colic</term> <note>original: "colica"; severe abdominal pain</note> and all cold winds <note>internal gas or flatulence, thought in humoral medicine to be "cold" and cause blockages</note> which cause discomfort in the urine, an affliction called <term>strangury</term> <note>original: "stranguria"; slow, painful, or interrupted urination</note>; the chilled womb <note>original: "Mutter"; literally "mother," the standard Early Modern term for the uterus</note> finds comfort through it, and it prevents its rising <note>original: "Aufsteigen"; referring to "the rising of the mother" or hysteria, where the uterus was believed to migrate upward in the body</note>, promotes the period of women, called the <term>menstruation</term> <note>original: "menstruum"</note>, when taken with lemon balm or motherwort water; taken with acorn water, it drives away the raging sores that are stirred up through the outlet of the human member <note>likely referring to venereal ulcers or infections of the genitals</note>, defends against all ailments of the kidneys and sets them right again, and awakens an enticement to human pleasure and desire in both men and women, makes the heart joyful, renews the blood, and restores everything that has fallen into decline through sadness, promotes the seed of nature <note>fertility or reproductive fluids</note> in man and woman, and taken in a good <term>Malmsey wine</term> <note>original: "Malvasir"; a sweet, high-alcohol wine originally from Greece, often used as a solvent for medicines</note>, it brings <term>delight</term> <note>original: "delectationem"</note> and venereal desire even in old age, also strengthening all the limbs and the whole body, especially when used often by elderly persons.

A beautiful green salt can also be made from copper, but it is not described or mentioned here in this book at this time.

### Of the Salt of Mars.
<note>original: "sal Martis"; the alchemical salt derived from iron</note>

The salt from iron is good for the <term>bloody flux</term> <note>original: "rohten Ruhr"; an old term for severe diarrhea with blood</note> and the disease called <term>dysentery</term> <note>original: "dysenteria"</note> when taken with wine vinegar and a little <term>oil of vitriol</term> <note>original: "olei vitrioli"; concentrated sulfuric acid, used in highly diluted medicinal preparations</note>; its weight is five or six <term>grains</term> <note>original: "Gran"</note> according to the individual's condition. When mixed with <term>virgin honey</term> <note>high-quality, pure honey that flows naturally from the comb</note>, it draws out all <term>abscesses</term> <note>original: "Apostemen"</note> and poisonous boils and cures them thoroughly.

This salt, taken in noble wine, produces good blood and restores that which was previously frail; it strengthens the memory and drives away the trembling in the limbs. Its weight consists of six grains if the weakness is mild; otherwise, the patient may well use up to a <term>quinte</term> <note>original: "Quintlein"; roughly 3.6 grams</note> of this salt.

## Of the *Salt of Mars* <note>original: "sal Martis"; refers to the salt of iron, named after the Roman god of war and the planet associated with that metal</note>.

The salt derived from iron is good for the "red flux" <note>bloody diarrhea</note> and the disease called *dysentery* <note>original: "dysenteria"; an inflammatory infection of the intestines</note> when taken with wine vinegar and a small amount of *oil of vitriol* <note>original: "olei vitrioli"; a historical name for sulfuric acid, used here in highly diluted medicinal preparations</note>. The dose is five or six <term>grains</term> <note>a small unit of weight, roughly 0.06 grams</note>, depending on the person's physical condition. This salt also strengthens the stomach, as it helps digest food very quickly. It stops the <term>monthly period</term> <note>original: "menstruum"</note> of women, as well as all <term>fluxes of the belly</term> <note>diarrhea</note> and similar passages. Mixed with <term>virgin honey</term> <note>original: "Jungfrauhonig"; honey that flows naturally from the comb without pressing</note>, it draws out all <term>abscesses</term> <note>original: "Apostemen"</note> and poisonous boils and cures them thoroughly.

## Of the *Salt of Jupiter* <note>original: "sal Jovis"; refers to the salt of tin, named after the king of the gods and the planet Jupiter</note>.

The salt derived from tin is good for the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: "hinfallende Sucht"; a historical term for epilepsy</note>. It drives away <term>melancholy</term> <note>original: "melancholiam"; believed to be caused by an excess of "black bile," resulting in gloominess or depression</note> and all dizziness of the head. It disperses the "heated blood" that attacks the heart and causes distress. It also drives away the <term>fluids</term> <note>original: "Flüsse"; or humors</note> that have risen into the head and seek an exit through the eyes or other places after <term>bloodletting</term> <note>original: "Aderlassen"; the medical practice of withdrawing blood to balance the humors</note>. This salt, when taken in <term>aged wine</term> <note>original: "firnem Wein"</note>, produces good blood and restores that which was previously frail. It strengthens the memory and drives away trembling in the limbs. Its dose consists of six grains when the weakness is mild; otherwise, the patient may well use up to a <term>quinten</term> <note>original: "Quintlein"; a historical German weight equivalent to about 3.6 to 4 grams</note> of this salt.

## How one should make the salt of antimony <note>original: "sal antimonii"</note> :

Take good Hungarian <term>antimony ore</term> <note>original: "Spießglas"; stibnite, the natural mineral form of antimony sulfide</note>, grind it very fine and subtle like flour, and <term>calcine</term> <note>original: "calcinirs"; to heat a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to change its physical or chemical state, usually to a powder</note> it over a gentle coal fire, as is customary, stirring it constantly with an iron rod until it has become quite whitish and no longer smokes, but can easily endure a rather strong heat. Then, put it into a <term>crucible</term> <note>original: "Schmelztiegel"; a heat-resistant container used for melting materials</note>, place it in the fire and melt it so that a beautiful, transparent yellow glass comes from it. Grind this glass very small again, put it into a <term>flask</term> <note>original: "Kolben-Glas"; a round-bottomed glass vessel with a long neck</note>, and pour a good, strong, distilled wine vinegar over it. Let it stand in gentle warmth, so the vinegar draws the **tincture of antimony** <note>original: "tinctura antimonii"</note> into itself and becomes deeply colored. This tincture or extraction of antimony can then be prepared further and used in other ways with great and excellent benefit.

When the tincture has been entirely extracted and the vinegar will no longer color itself, then dry the remaining powder very well, which will be black. Grind an equal weight of yellow common sulfur into it, put it into a crucible, well <term>luted</term> <note>original: "verlutirt"; sealed with a clay or paste to make it airtight</note>, and let it stand in a moderate fire until the sulfur has burned away again. Then grind the remaining material small, and pour new distilled vinegar over it again—

## Of the Salt of Sulfur, and First How It Should Be Made.

<margin>Recipe</margin>Take one part common sulfur / half a part **salt of tartar** <term>sal tartari</term> <note>potassium carbonate derived from wine lees</note> / grind them small together / then set it upon a charcoal fire / and let it flow / until it has become quite red / once the **matter** <term>materia</term> has become red / grind it small / put it into a glass / pour **spirit of wine** <term>spiritum vini</term> <note>distilled alcohol</note> upon it / let it stand thus in a subtle heat / until the **spirit of wine** has become blood-red like a ruby / thus you have the **tincture of sulfur** <term>tincturam sulphuris</term> mixed with the **salt of tartar** / when such a **tincture** is separated from the salt of tartar / and is further prepared into its **state** <term>statum</term> / it also performs its function; continue now with the extraction of the **spirit of wine** so often and so long / until the **spirit** will no longer take on color / or no further color reveals itself / nor any of the salt of tartar is tasted in the **spirit of wine**; The **matter** which remains behind / **reverberate** <term>reverberir</term> <note>to heat in a furnace where the flames are reflected back onto the matter, often to oxidize or calcine it</note> day and night continuously, quite subtly and gently, being well sealed / then grind the **matter** small again / and extract the salt as from other things / also with distilled vinegar / draw the vinegar off from it / and sweeten <note>original: "süsse"; in alchemy, to "sweeten" or edulcorate means to wash away acids or salts with water</note> the salt / which remains at the bottom with **spirit of wine**, or common distilled rain-water / through frequent repetition of the distillation / until it has become beautifully clear and white / then it is prepared.

### Concerning Rock Salt <term>Sal gemmae</term>

Rock salt <term>Sal gemmae</term> <note>original: *sal gemmæ*, a pure mineral salt often found in transparent, gem-like crystals</note> is used more externally than internally. Taken internally, it provides a decent cooling effect, but it is not to be compared to saltpeter <term>Salpeter</term>, for in rock salt the efficacy is lesser. Externally, however, it yields nothing to saltpeter, especially when used on old sores. Its best method for external use is as follows:

Take one part finely ground antimony <term>antimonium</term>, half a part rock salt <term>sal gemmæ</term>, and as much brick dust <term>Ziegelmehl</term> as the weight of the material itself; then add three times as much in brick chunks, so that the weight of the chunks equals that of the brick dust. Grind and mix it all together, and distill it through a retort so that the spirits <term>spiritus</term> <note>volatile vapors captured during distillation</note> are retained. First, a water will come over. Eventually, the water will flow in such a way that if you hold an iron spoon beneath it and let the drops fall in, it will turn white like milk <note>a chemical indicator of a change in the distillate's composition</note>. When you see this sign, remove the receiver and put another one in its place; seal it well with lute <note>a clay or paste used to make the glass joints airtight</note> and increase the fire further. Do not lose heart! Then the yellow oil <term>oleum</term> comes, which is very heavy and dense <term>ponderirt</term>. 

If one puts this oil into a flask and sets it in sand <term>arenam</term> <note>original: *arenam*, a sand bath used to distribute heat evenly to the glass</note>, and gives it a good, strong fire for half a day, the oil coagulates into a brown stone. Grind this small and dissolve <term>solvir</term> it on a glass plate in a cellar; a transparent oil will come from it, or a liquid <term>liquor</term> like a ruby. When this is brushed over old, foul sores, as well as new injuries, it creates a good foundation for healing and can drive away many open, foul, and long-lasting wounds, provided that a proper wound-drink <term>Wundtranck</term> <note>an internal herbal tonic used to support healing from the inside out</note> is used alongside it. For this is the fundamental and primary aim when dealing with all corrupted matters—

### Concerning Common Table Salt

Common table salt <term>Speise-Saltz</term> by its nature, through daily use and consumption, provokes carnal desire; for this reason, **Plutarch** <note>original: *Plutarchus*, the Greek-Roman historian and philosopher</note> writes that the Egyptians had to be moderate in their salt consumption. Through a special method, a fragrant **spirit** <term>spiritus</term> is driven out from common salt, the weight of which is prescribed at only 3 or 4 grains. Taken with wine or another suitable water, and used with diligent persistence, it **dissolves** <term>resolvirt</term> the bladder stone and drives it out completely—especially when taken with parsley water or the water distilled from the little black berries that grow on ivy. It is also effective for gout, as it separates clotted blood from one another when it tries to form a **clotting** <term>coagulation</term> in the veins due to great, unnatural, and persistent heat, from which paralysis and **stiffness** <term>contractur</term> <note>original: *contractur*, the permanent shortening of a muscle or joint</note> can arise. For every **dissolved substance** <term>resolvirte Materia</term> draws to itself the **clotted substance** <term>coagulirte Materia</term> of its own kind; therefore, one stone can break another. ### Fifth Part of the Last Testament

Take one pound of salt, well-dried; half a pound of sal ammoniac (<term>Salmiac</term>); one pound of sulfur; one pound of <term>antimony</term> <note>original: *antimonium*, a metallic mineral used in early medicine and alchemy</note>; and one pound of quicklime. This same oil, when <term>rectified with spirits of wine</term> <note>original: *spiritu vini rectificiret*; purified by distilling it with strong alcohol</note>, becomes exceedingly beautiful. Its dosage is five or six drops to be taken with aged wine. ### Alumen plumosum or Plume Alum.

This is a fixed salt <note>original: *fixes Saltz*; in alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that resists the action of fire and does not easily evaporate</note>. Little can be written regarding its virtues for internal use; however, externally it dries out all bad flows <note>original: *Flüsse*; referring to "humors" or discharges from the body</note> and afflictions of wounds. When strewn into them, it stills the bleeding of wounds and the joint-water <note>original: *Gliedwasser*; likely referring to synovial fluid or serous discharge from a wound</note>.

### Borax.

This salt is not corrosive, as other salts are, but is rather a "sweet" salt. Externally, this salt is not used particularly much, but internally it brings about a binding <note>original: *Verstopffung*; here meaning it acts as an astringent to stop diarrhea, rather than causing a harmful blockage</note>. For this purpose, you should take one *quintlein* <note>original: *quent*; a historical German weight of about 3.6 grams</note> of it, one *quintlein* of **Crocus of Mars** <note>original: *crocum martis*; an alchemical term for iron oxide or rust, used medicinally</note>, one *quintlein* of finely pounded nutmeg, as well as **Sealed Earth** <note>original: *terra sigillata*; a medicinal clay from specific regions, traditionally stamped with a seal to prove its authenticity</note>, pomegranates, and **carob** <note>original: *Johannesbrod*; literally "St. John's Bread"</note>, each likewise finely pounded. These are to be baked into a small cake with unsalted butter and one egg until quite dry. When given to the patient to eat, it prevents the breakthrough of the salt of the disease **dysentery** or the "bloody flux" <note>original: *rohten Ruhr*; a historical term for severe, bloody diarrhea</note>, if used for the third time.

## Tartar, Cream of Tartar.

Many kinds of medicines are prepared from tartar <note>original: *Weinstein*; a sediment found in wine barrels, used widely in alchemy and early medicine</note>, for both internal and external use; however, I will now write only of the most prominent ones and report on those that have proven themselves in experience and have demonstrated their efficacy. First, however, a liquid <note>original: *liquor*</note> is made from it: the tartar is put into a pot and calcined <note>burned at high temperatures to reduce it to a mineral ash</note> in a blast furnace <note>original: *Wind-Ofen*; a furnace designed to create a strong natural draft for high heat</note> until it is burned white. Afterward, it is ground finely, placed on a stone in a cellar, put into a pointed wool bag, and hung up; thus the liquid flows out, which you should catch in a glass. This is the common method known to everyone. This liquid is good for all injuries that have not yet become too severe; it brings about a healing, cleanses mangy skin and scabs <note>original: *Kräße*; a term for itchy skin eruptions or scabies</note>, makes the skin smooth and clean, and dispels tetters <note>original: *Zittrachten*; archaic term for various skin diseases like ringworm or eczema</note> and lichens on the hands when smeared upon them.

Give it a good fire so that the matter flows well, keeping it glowing for one hour. ## Magistery of Tartar.

<note>original: *Magisterium tartari*; in alchemy, a "magistery" is a preparation where the essence of a substance is purified and concentrated to its highest medicinal state.</note>

Take white calcined tartar, grind it small, put it into a flask, and pour a good **spirit of wine** <term>spiritus vini: high-proof distilled alcohol or ethanol</term> over it; distill off the phlegm <note>the watery, inactive part of the distillate</note>, so the spirit remains behind in the tartar; pour new spirit over it and distill that off as well; do this as often as necessary until the tartar has become completely full of the spirit and can take in no more, but rather lets it go again during distillation; then grind the prepared tartar small and treat it as mentioned before, and let it dissolve; if the solution is one part, then add two parts of spirit of wine to it; circulate <note>a process of continuous heat and condensation in a sealed vessel, intended to "ripen" the medicine</note> it for two months; thus the tartar loses its sharpness and corrosive nature. Administering ten or twelve grains of this Magistery promotes urine, cleanses the blood, expels dropsy <note>original: *Wassersucht*; swelling caused by fluid retention</note>, breaks up bladder stones, and serves against gout <note>original: *Podagra*; specifically gout affecting the foot</note>.

## Water of Tartar.

Take raw tartar <note>the potassium bitartrate sediment found in wine barrels</note> and saltpeter <note>potassium nitrate</note>, an equal amount of each rubbed together, and take an earthenware flask <term>kolben: a round-bottomed distillation vessel</term> that has a hollow tube or a breathing-hole <note>original: "spiraculum"</note> at the back; place it in a distillation furnace in the open fire, with a glass head <term>helm: the cap of a still (alembic) that collects and directs vapors</term> on top; also seal a receiver <note>the vessel that collects the distillate</note> to it with lute. When the flask has become red-hot, then throw several glowing coals into the flask through the hollow tube. When this is done, take a spoonful of the ground material and pour it into the flask onto the coals; the material will then ignite and give off a great vapor. Plug the tube tightly with a wet rag. When the vapor has condensed, then add more material into the flask and plug it again; repeat this as often and for as long as it takes until you have distilled all the material. In this way, you will obtain a beautiful, transparent, golden-yellow water, without any corrosive quality.

This water is safe and good to use both internally and externally; taken internally, a spoonful of it cools and promotes the flow of urine and creates good digestion. Externally, it soothes both old and fresh wounds when washed with it and provides the cause for healing.

# Fifth Part of the Last Testament.

## Balsam of Tartar.

Take white calcined <note>Calcination is the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to remove impurities or change its chemical state.</note> tartar <note>original: "Weinstein"; the potassium bitartrate sediment from wine barrels</note>, grind it small, put it into a glass flask, and pour a strong *aqua fortis* <term>aqua fort: literally "strong water," a corrosive mineral acid, typically nitric acid</term> over it, distilled from one part vitriol <term>vitriol: a sulfate mineral, often iron or copper sulfate</term>, one part saltpeter <term>salpeter: potassium nitrate</term>, a half part alum, and a fourth part verdigris <term>Grünspan: the green crust that forms on copper, used here for its chemical properties</term>. Distill the water from it; thus the phlegm <note>the watery, inactive portion of a distillate</note> passes over, but the spirits remain behind in the tartar. Pour new water over it and distill it off again; do this several times until the tartar can no longer absorb any spirits but instead lets them pass again. After this, take the prepared tartar, grind it small again on a marble stone, and place it in a cellar to dissolve <note>original: "solviren"; specifically referring to deliquescence, where a salt absorbs moisture from the damp cellar air until it turns into a liquid</note> as previously mentioned, so that it flows into a liquor. Take one part of this clear liquor and two parts of fresh, pure tree oil <note>original: "Baum-öhl"; usually referring to olive oil</note>, and cook them well together in a flask. Thus a balsam will be made from it, to which—in the case of incurable, old, evil, stinking, and corrosive <note>original: "um sich fressenden"; literally "eating around itself," referring to spreading ulcers or gangrenous sores</note> sores, whatever they may be or however they may be named—nothing can be compared.

This is as much as I wished to describe and report regarding tartar at this time. Therefore, I will proceed <note>original: "pergiren," from the Latin *pergere*</note> and continue, to teach and report how to extract and prepare the salts <note>original: "Salia"</note> from all other vegetables <note>original: "vegetabilien"; meaning the plant kingdom in general</note> and herbs, and how they may be usefully employed in the medicine of man. But first, I must point out and report that all vegetable salts, after their extraction, can be brought to a state where, through frequent repetition of the solution, they crystallize <note>original: "schießen"; literally "shoot" into crystals</note> in the cold to be quite beautifully transparent, pure, clear, and white, like a fine transparent refined saltpeter, sugar candy, or white vitriol. For vegetables have just as much...

...their vitriol <term>vitriol: a sulfate mineral, considered by alchemists to be a primary "seed" or acidic principle of metals</term> within themselves / just as minerals and all metals do / which have their origin for the most part from a vitriolic essence / as can be seen from the fact that all metals, after their destruction, are brought back again into a natural vitriol / which provides the first coagulation <note>Coagulation is the process of a liquid becoming a solid or semi-solid state; here, the "birth" of a metal from a liquid mineral solution.</note> of the metal / of which I have already given indication and report in the preceding books and parts / likewise all small stones / crystals, and salts from herbs are to be compared to a vitriolic vegetable essence / as can be proven by experience / and every understanding person will be able to comprehend; The salts <note>original: "Salia"</note> of herbs, however, are extracted as follows:

## How the salts are to be extracted from all herbs and vegetables.

Take whichever herb you wish / burn it to ashes / make a lye <note>A liquid solution made by soaking ashes in water, used here to dissolve the soluble salts from the plant matter.</note> from it with warm water / coagulate the lye <note>Evaporate the water so that the solid matter remains.</note> / so the salt remains at the bottom / dissolve that in spirit of wine <term>spiritu vini: highly concentrated alcohol or ethanol</term>, the dregs <note>original: "feces"; the solid impurities or sediment that settle out of a solution</note> which will settle / throw away / draw off the spirit of wine by distillation <note>original: "distillationem"; the process of heating a liquid to create vapor and then condensing it back into a liquid to purify it</note> / and dissolve it as many times / until the salt is beautiful, pure, and clear / and no more dregs settle / then it is finished. When one handles the purification with the spirit of wine correctly / all salts of herbs can be brought to such a state / so beautiful / clear / and pure / that they form into transparent crystals / like a clear / pure / refined saltpeter <term>salpeter: potassium nitrate, known for its distinct needle-like crystals</term>.

In this same way, the salt is also made from roots and every kind of wood / likewise from aromatics <term>aromatibus: aromatic substances, such as spices and fragrant resins</term> or seasonings.
