# USES

## Absinthe, Wormwood.

Salt of wormwood <note>Wormwood salt was typically made by calcining (burning) the plant and extracting the potassium-rich ash.</note> promotes the flow of urine, expels colic, settles wind [gas] in the body, and promotes sweating. It is good for all long-lasting fevers, consumes the "evil" in the stomach <note>Likely referring to indigestion or acidic buildup.</note>, creates an appetite for eating, and cleanses the blood. It is effective when used during times of pestilence [the plague] if a half quinte <term>quinte: a historical unit of weight, approximately 3.7 grams</term> is taken every morning in aged wine <note>original: "firnem Wein"</note> and followed by sweating. Externally, use this salt with white lead and a little tree oil [olive oil] to make a small salve; apply it with cotton or scraped wool from linen cloth onto fig-warts <note>A contemporary term for hemorrhoids or similar skin growths.</note> and similar sores; it heals such things completely.

## Borago, Borage.

Creates good blood and strengthens the heart. It is good for tertian and quartan fevers <note>Types of recurring fevers associated with malaria.</note> and expels all evil through sweat <note>original: "per sudorem"</note>, just like the salt of wormwood. Its dosage is also the same as the wormwood salt, taken in aged wine.

## Chamomilla, Chamomile.

Promotes menstruation <note>original: "menstruum"</note> and urine, expels bladder stones, and remedies all ailments of the liver. Its dosage is the same as described above, taken in aged wine.

## Angelica, Angelica.

Serves against the pestilence [the plague] when a half quinte is taken with rue-vinegar and pressed juniper juice. Taken with anise oil, it renovates the blood, as well as the cerebrum or the brain, and expels all rheums <note>original: "Flüsse"; refers to the discharge of fluid or "catarrh" believed to flow from the brain according to the theory of the four humors.</note> of the head.

## Artemisia, Mugwort.

Two drachmas <term>drachma: a unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</term> taken with five or six drops of oil of myrrh or **juniper oil** <note>original: "oleo juniperi"</note> in wine, expels and breaks the stone [kidney or bladder stones], promotes the flow of urine, and opens the closed womb <note>original: "Mutter"; in early modern medicine, the "closed" womb was thought to cause various systemic illnesses.</note>.

## Betonica, Betony.

One quinte <term>quinte: a historical unit of weight, approximately 3.7 grams</term> taken in wine expels any poison that a person has ingested; it also serves to treat kidney ailments and, when applied externally as a poultice or dusted upon a wound, treats the bites of venomous animals.

## Hypericum, St. John’s Wort.

Promotes urine and **menstruation** <note>original: "menstruum"</note> when taken with lemon balm water. Six or eight grains <term>grain: the smallest unit of weight, approximately 0.06 grams</term> taken with boiled speedwell water <note>original: "Ehrenpreis-Wasser"</note> acts as a **preventative** <note>original: "præservativ"</note> for all wounds; furthermore, if **St. John’s Wort oil** <note>original: "oleum hypericonis"</note> is rubbed on externally, it heals them completely.

## Pimpinella, Burnet.

Its salt serves to treat old injuries and heals wonderfully; it also serves against the pestilence [the plague], stills a woman’s period or **menstruation** <note>original: "menstruum"</note>, and the "red flux" <note>original: "rothe Ruhr"; a historical term for dysentery.</note>. It cleanses the blood, lungs, liver, and kidneys, and is used against the "rising of the womb" <note>original: "Aufsteigen der Mutter"; a condition where the uterus was believed to move upward in the body, causing respiratory or emotional distress, often called hysteria.</note>.

## Rosmarinus, Rosemary.

Half a quinte taken in wine strengthens the heart, brain, and all limbs; it creates an appetite for eating and provides good digestion.

## Guajacum, Guaiac (French Wood).

When the water, **liquid** <note>original: "liquor"</note>, and the oil are distilled from the wood in a **dry bath** <note>original: "balneo sicco"; a method of heating a vessel using sand or ashes rather than water.</note>, the wood becomes

### Persicaria, Water-Pepper.

The salt of **Water-Pepper** <note>original: "Persicaria"</note> is a magnificent **secret remedy** <term>arcanum: a secret or powerful medicinal formula</term> for old, rotten, foul-smelling wounds, as well as for cancer, fistulas, "the wolf" <note>original: "Wolff"; a historical term for lupus or similar eating sores.</note>, "siren" <note>original: "Siren"; likely a skin condition or ulcer.</note>, lichen, and skin eruptions <note>original: "Zitrachten"; likely referring to tetter or scaly skin conditions.</note> when sprinkled on externally. However, for internal use, also use a good "wound-drink" made as follows: Take one and a half lot <term>lot: a pre-metric unit of weight, roughly 14–17 grams</term> of rhubarb, 2 lot of calamus <note>sweet flag</note>, five handfuls of soapwort, and one lot each of myrrh, mastic, and frankincense, and one lot of violet root. Boil or cook these well in common water, then pour off the liquid until clear, and dissolve four lot of this salt within it. When used, it demonstrates its virtue and power with wondrous effect on all wounds.

### Salvia, Sage.

It draws the blood out of wounds and cleanses bad sores when applied externally; one quinte taken in wine in the morning creates good blood internally and makes the heart joyful.

## *Scordium*, Water Germander or Leek-Garlic.

Serves against poisonous snake bites; promotes urine; taken with wine in the amount of two **drachmas** <term>drachma: a unit of weight, approximately 3.9 grams</term>, it gives the stomach good digestion and is useful for **hernias** <note>original: "Durchbruch"; historically referring to a rupture or hernia.</note>.

## *Caryophyllata*, Herb Bennet.

Strengthens the **memory** <note>original: "memoria"</note>, serves for jaundice; promotes sweat and urine; is usefully employed for those with **dropsy** <term>dropsy: a historical term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</term>; creates good blood; dispels sadness; prevents **stroke** <note>original: "Schlag"; can refer to a stroke, seizure, or sudden paralysis.</note> and fosters cheerful thoughts when a half **quinte** <term>quinte: a historical unit of weight, approximately 3.7 grams</term> is taken in **spirit of wine** <note>original: "spiritu vini"; ethanol or high-proof distilled alcohol.</note>. Externally, it heals and cleanses all **canker sores** <note>original: "Mundfäule"; literally "mouth rot," referring to oral infections or ulcers.</note>, as well as **scurvy** <term>scurvy: a disease caused by Vitamin C deficiency, often affecting the gums and mouth</term> and the like.

## *Foeniculum*, Fennel.

A half quinte used with endive water promotes **menstruation** <note>original: "der Frauen Zeit"; literally "women's time."</note>; stills the unnatural heat of the stomach; breaks up clotted blood in the body; opens obstructions of the spleen and the liver; consumes all phlegmatic moisture that causes harm to the **vision** <note>original: "Gesicht"</note>; and dispels wheezing and heavy breathing. Externally, it heals all spider, scorpion, and snake bites.

## *Hyssopus*, Hyssop.

Promotes urination; promotes **menstruation** <note>original: "der Weiber Zeit"</note>; is good to use for the lungs and **shortness of breath** <note>original: "Engbrüstigkeit"; literally "narrow-breastedness," referring to asthma or respiratory congestion.</note>; it is also a **preventative** <note>original: "conservativ"</note> against stroke, taken at the weight of twelve **barleycorns** <term>barleycorn: a traditional unit of weight, approximately 0.05 grams</term> with six or eight drops of **juniper oil** <note>original: "oleo juniperi"</note> in a good spirit of wine or **water of life** <note>original: "aqua vitæ"; a strong distilled spirit.</note>.

## *Juniperus*, Juniper Tree.

The salt extracted from the wood, root, and berry or fruit stills the griping <note>original: "Krimmen"; refers to sharp, cramping abdominal pains or colic.</note> in the body, promotes urine, crushes bladder stones, and expels grit and sand. When six or eight grains are dissolved in its own oil, and eight or ten drops are taken with a spoonful of its own water or parsley water, it is also good for **dropsy** <term>dropsy: a historical term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</term>, and promotes the flow during a woman’s suppressed period <note>original: "Verstopffung der Weiber Zeit"; referring to delayed or obstructed menstruation.</note>.

Applied externally, dissolved in warm wine-vinegar and held warm in the mouth, it draws out the pain of toothache; it also serves internally, as mentioned above, for <term>podagra</term> <note>original: "Podagra"; a historical term for gout, particularly when it affects the joints of the foot.</note>.

## *Faba suilla*, Henbane.

Stills the excessive flows of women; induces sleep; when half a <term>quent</term> <note>original: "Quent"; a historical unit of weight, approximately 3.7 to 4 grams.</note> is used in rose water, it also draws out the heat of **quinsy** <term>quinsy: a historical term (German: *Bräune*) for severe, often suffocating, inflammation of the throat or tonsils</term>, when the throat is gargled with it.

## *Laurus*, Laurel Tree.

The salt from the leaves of the laurel tree, and also from its fruit, expels the **French disease** <term>French disease: a common historical name for syphilis</term>, when taken with the boiled water of <term>lignum guaiacum</term> <note>original: "ligno Guajaco"; "holy wood" from the Caribbean, which was the standard 16th-century treatment for syphilis.</note> in the amount of half a quinte; it consumes the rheums of the head <note>original: "Hauptflüsse"; literally "head-flows," referring to the excess phlegm or "catarrh" that humoral medicine believed flowed from the brain to cause illness elsewhere.</note>, stills the griping in the body, dispels the stone, and removes **jaundice** <note>original: "Lebersucht"; literally "liver-sickness," usually referring to jaundice or chronic liver disorders.</note>; externally, it is good for spider and scorpion bites.

## *Ruta*, Rue.

Resists the pains of **consumption** <term>consumption: a historical term for wasting diseases, most commonly pulmonary tuberculosis</term>; it is good for pain in the side; eases heavy breathing; leads

## *Juglans*, **Walnut Tree.**

The salt from the walnut shells, taken in a dose of eight or nine grains with spirit of wine, breaks the bladder stone and is good for gout.

## *Triticum*, **Wheat.**

Four **lot** <term>lot: a historical unit of weight, approximately 15 to 16 grams</term> of this salt mixed with twelve lot of sourdough made from its own flour, and then applied as a plaster every evening and morning, heals all **shingles** <note>original: "Zittermahlen"</note>, skin eruptions, and inflammation of women’s breasts; likewise, it treats the bites of poisonous snakes and also opens **corns** <note>original: "Kräen-Augen"; literally "crow's eyes"</note> on the feet and all sores.

### *Triticum*, **Wheat.**

Four **lot** <term>lot: a historical unit of weight, approximately 15-18 grams</term> of this salt mixed with twelve lot of sourdough made from its own flour and blended together, then applied in the manner of a plaster <note>original: "Pflastersweise"</note> evening and morning, heals all shingles <note>original: "Zittermahlen"</note>, lichens, and inflammation of women’s breasts; likewise the bites of venomous snakes; it also opens corns <note>original: "Kräen-Augen"; literally "crow's eyes"</note> on the feet and all sores.

Fr. Basilii Valentini <note>Brother Basil Valentine, the legendary alchemist and monk.</note>

# Licorice <note>original: *Glycyrrhiza*, *Süßholtz*</note>.

The salt derived from licorice wood is useful for many ailments <note>original: *Bresten*</note>; used especially with its own juice in a dose of six grains <note>a small unit of weight, roughly 0.06 grams</note>, it dispels lung disease <note>original: *Lungensucht*</note>, from which long-lasting coughs and consumption <note>original: *Schwindsucht*, a historical term for tuberculosis</note> arise. It also protects the liver, bladder, and kidneys from all afflictions; it makes the stomach receptive to food and drink, and dispels severe strangury <note>original: *Harnwinde*, a condition of painful or difficult urination</note>.

# Kali, a herb so named.

This grows on the shores of the sea and the coastal sands, especially in Zealand <note>likely referring to the coastal province in the Netherlands</note>, as well as in other places where salt springs and salt wells occur. Wherever this herb is found, it is surely a good sign that true veins of salt are present. It is called "Zealand wall-pepper" by some; the Dutch call it *Crabbequel* <note>Glasswort or Samphire</note>. It has a straight, strong, and round stem, with thick, fatty, and succulent leaves. Among all herbs, there is no salt more closely related to common table salt than this salt; therefore, it is comparable to common salt in all its virtues and powers. Should it be necessary, due to a lack or deficiency of common salt, this can well be used in food and everything else in its stead.

# Concerning spices <note>original: *De aromatibus*</note>.

When the essential oils <note>original: *Olitäten*</note> have been distilled from the spices, the residue <note>original: *residuum*</note> is placed in a pot and burnt to ashes. Then their salts <note>original: *salia*</note> are extracted with spirit of wine <note>original: *spiritu vini*, i.e., alcohol</note>, just as was done with the herbs.

Fifth Part of the Last Testament

->Usage.<-

### Sweet Flag <note>original: *Acorus*, *Calmus*</note>.

Anyone afflicted with heart palpitations should drink six grains <note>a very small unit of weight, roughly 0.06 grams</note> of this salt in half a *Lot* <note>a historical unit of weight; half a *Lot* is approximately 7-8 grams</note> of cinnamon water. It also dispels fever and creates a well-digesting stomach. Taken every morning in this manner, it aids digestion and consumes the "evil" <note>referring to impurities or bad humors</note> in the stomach, creates good blood, strengthens the limbs, and brings good breath.

### Pepper <note>original: *Piper*, *Pfeffer*</note>.

The salt of pepper, with four or five grains taken in spirits of wine <note>original: *spiritu vini*, high-proof distilled alcohol</note>, consumes all evil moisture of the stomach, warms it, and stills fever. Pepper-salt dissolved in vinegar and held warm in the mouth stills toothaches and draws all phlegm from the jaws; applied to wounds, it cleanses them and heals all injuries.

### Ginger <note>original: *Zingiber*, *Ingwer*</note>.

Two grains placed in six drops of its oil and taken with a little warm wine in the evening when one wishes to go to sleep, consumes all evil moisture of the stomach, dispels fever, and brings the stomach to proper digestion. It warms all the limbs and consumes all their evil, cold moisture <note>in the medical theory of the time, "cold moisture" was thought to cause sluggishness and joint pain</note>.

### Zedoary <note>original: *Zedoaria*, *Zitwarwurtz*; a root related to ginger and turmeric</note>.

Six grains of this salt taken with rue-vinegar <note>vinegar infused with the herb Rue, often used as a disinfectant</note> counteracts all poison and is good against the pestilence <note>the plague</note>. It serves people who are of a "cold nature" <note>referring to the Galenic theory of temperaments</note>; used often in aged wine <note>original: *firnem Wein*</note>, it brings a desire for eating and gives the stomach good digestion.

## Cloves <note>original: *Caryophyllon*, *Negelein*</note>.

Two grains of clove-salt dissolved in half a *Quentlein* <note>a historical small unit of weight, approximately 3.6 grams</note> of fennel water, and placed into weak eyes, creates good vision and clears the eyes. Six grains taken with wine warms the stomach, produces good digestion, strengthens the heart, and is beneficial for the liver. Two or three grains taken in wine with eight or ten drops of its distilled oil protects against internal rot <note>referring to infection, sepsis, or the corruption of humors</note> and creates good, sweet-smelling breath. Used externally on old injuries, it establishes a foundation for healing.

## Nutmeg <note>original: *Nux moschata*, *Muscatnuß*</note> and the salt from the mace <note>original: *Muscatenblumen*</note> have one power.

Three or four grains used in wine with eight or six drops of its oil strengthens all of a person’s limbs. Likewise, it is also good for heart tremors and for fainting.

## Cinnamon Bark <note>original: *Cinamomum*, *Zimmetrinden*</note>.

Two or three spoons full of this salt taken in its own water <note>a distilled hydrosol of cinnamon</note> with two or three drops of oil of cinnamon <note>original: *olei cinamomi*</note> strengthens the heart and all the vital spirits of a person; it expels a stillbirth and provides great assistance to those in difficult labor; it also drives away the afterbirth <term>the placenta; Latin: *secundinam*</term>, corrects a "stopped-up womb" <note>likely referring to menstrual blockages or uterine stagnation</note>, creates good blood, and preserves the person from rot.

# Fifth Part of the Last Testament

## On the Salt of Animals.

->And first:<-

### How one should make the salt from the simple mummy <term>a substance prepared from the remains of a human body, believed to contain concentrated vital life force; original: *Mumia*</term>, or from the human body, as well as from the flesh of all other animals.

When a person—one who is not infected with any "evil blood" <note>likely referring to venereal diseases or leprosy</note> and is between eighteen and twenty-four years of age—is executed by the sword, or is otherwise fatally wounded in the heart, collect the blood and dry it in an oven. From the body, take out the entire heart, as well as the areas where the muscles have their seat and dwelling; have the flesh cut out and dry it likewise in an oven. Afterward, take the bones and have them removed from the limbs and arms, along with the marrow that is within them, and the empty, detached brain-pan or skull. Burn the bones, including the skull, in a sealed pot until they are entirely reduced to ashes. Rub them into a fine powder and pour a good spirit of wine <term>distilled alcohol; original: *spiritum vini*</term> over them. Let the spirit stand, thus sealed, for fourteen days in gentle heat; swirl it once or several times every day in the glass. Pour off the spirit of wine cleanly and filter it clear through waste-paper <note>original: *Maculatur-Papyr*; used in early modern laboratories as a filter</note>. In this way, you have the salt from human bones <note>original Latin: *sal ex ossibus hominis*</note> within the spirit of wine.

Mince the dried heart, flesh, and blood very small; pour this prepared spirit of wine over them and let it digest <note>to steep in a controlled heat</note> for one month, well-sealed. Afterward, distill the spirit of wine away from it. That material which remains in the bottom <note>original Latin: *in fundo*</note>, place into a pot, seal it with lute <note>original: *verlutirs*; a paste made of clay and other materials to airtight-seal alchemical vessels</note>, and 
burn <note>This is the catchword "brenn," indicating the start of the following page.</note>

<summary>This page provides gruesome instructions for preparing "human salt" or alchemical mummy from the body of a young, healthy person who died a violent death. It details the separate processing of blood, flesh, and bone through drying, calcination, and extraction with alcohol.</summary>
<keywords>Mumia, human salt, calcination, spirit of wine, distillation, alchemical anatomy, Paracelsian medicine</keywords>

# Fr. Basilius Valentinus.

Burn it in a potter's or brickmaker's kiln until it is entirely reduced to ashes. Then, place it, finely pulverized, into a glass flask; pour the previously distilled spirit of wine <term>distilled alcohol; original: *spiritum vini*</term> over it again. Let it stand for fourteen days in a warm place, and swirl it every day. Finally, pour off the spirit of wine and filter it clear through waste-paper <note>original: *Maculatur-Papyr*; commonly used in early modern laboratories for filtration</note>. Afterward, distill it off in the ash-bath <note>a method of heating a vessel by surrounding it with hot ashes to provide even, gentle heat</note>, so that the salt of man <term>human salt; original: *sal hominis*</term> remains at the bottom <note>original: *in fundo*</note>, or at the base of the glass. Dissolve <note>original: *resolvir*</note> this same salt again in fresh spirit of wine. If it leaves behind any dregs <note>original: *feces*</note>, discard them and separate them; then coagulate the salt again through distillation <note>original: *per distillationem*</note>. This you can repeat several times and clarify the salt until it is as clear and transparent as a crystal. This is then the true salt of man prepared from the simple mummy <term>a substance prepared from the remains of a human body, believed to contain concentrated vital life force; original: *Mumia*</term>. For I am not speaking now of the embalmed mummy <note>referring to ancient Egyptian remains or resin-preserved bodies often imported for medicine</note> which is obtained from the shores of the sea or from the tombs of the deceased.

In this way, you can also make the salt from all other animals; and when they are slaughtered, collect the blood for this purpose as well, provided only that each species of animal be healthy and not burdened with excessive age.

### On the salt of urine <note>original: *sale urinæ*</note>.

The **salt** from urine is not to be esteemed as lowly / as some may suppose / but is an excellent **medicine** <note>original: *medicamentum*</note> to be used for many things / and is first prepared thus: Take urine / let it stand for a day or several / so that it settles well / when that has happened / then pour off the clear liquid / and separate the turbidity from it / put the clear, poured-off urine into a vessel / and boil it down dry until it becomes a stone / then take the salt / grind it small / and resolve <note>dissolve</note> it again in pure, fresh spring water / let all the impurities settle well / then pour off the clear liquid again / and separate the **dregs** <note>original: *feces*</note> and impurities from it / coagulate <note>solidify through evaporation</note> that which was poured off in a glass vessel until dry / then you have the **salt of urine** <note>original: *sal urinæ*</note>.

->Usage.<-

Its use is manifold, and all of its virtues have not yet been fully fathomed. The **salt of urine** <note>original: *sal urinæ*; primarily urea and ammonium salts extracted from fermented urine</note> alone is entirely volatile, whereas other salts, by contrast, are found to be stable and quite fixed; it prepares other mineral things so that they too may be brought to a state of volatility. **Saltpeter** <note>original: *Salniter*; potassium nitrate</note> also has a cause and a promotion to grow from the salt of urine of humans and other animals, since the "mother of saltpeter" <note>the nitrogen-rich earth or waste matter from which nitre was harvested</note> is fed by the salt of urine, and is nourished and sustained to promote its birth, so that the saltpeter can grow all the sooner and reach its augmentation.

However, to use this salt as a medicine, it is done thus: one takes a Quentchen <term>an old unit of weight, approximately 3.6 grams</term> of it, dissolved in **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritu vini*; high-proof alcohol</note>—or, even better, dissolved in **balsam of sulfur** <note>original: *balsamo sulphuris*; sulfur dissolved in oils</note>. This drives away **consumption** <note>original: *Schwindsucht*; a term for wasting diseases like tuberculosis</note> and heals all ailments of the lungs; it stills shortness of breath and settles the sharp pain in the side called **pleurisy** <note>original: *pleuresis*</note>. A bath is also made from this salt, along with other associated salts, which provides a softening effect, draws out [illness] excellently, and stills **gout** <note>original: *Podagra*; a painful form of inflammatory arthritis</note>, providing relief from that very hour, namely thus:

One takes six Stübichen <term>an old liquid measure, roughly 3.7 liters per unit</term> of warm water and dissolves within it six pounds of this salt and three pounds of **salt of tartar** <note>original: *salis tartari*; potassium carbonate derived from wine lees</note>. Let them come to a boil together, after which the hands or legs are held therein—as warm as one can endure it—for a period of time. If this is repeated three or four times, it draws out all the phlegm of the **coagulated matter** <note>original: *coagulirten Materia*; thickened bodily fluids believed in Galenic medicine to cause joint pain</note> from which gout takes its origin; it opens the pores and sweat-holes, and provides an excellent resolution of the hardening and internal

## Vulpes, the Fox.

When the salt is to be extracted from the fox, its lung must be used for that purpose. Its weight is half a **Quentchen** <term>an old unit of weight, approximately 3.6 grams</term>. Taken with a good **water of life** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*; high-proof distilled spirits</note>, it drives away madness and dizziness of the head. Used in this way, it also resists cramps; and when used with **balsam of sulfur** <note>original: *balsamo sulphuris*; sulfur dissolved in oil</note>, it heals **consumption** <note>original: *Lungensucht*; wasting lung disease</note>. Taken with ivy-water, it breaks the stone in the bladder and loins. It dries out all evil humors and brings back appetite and desire for human **pleasure** <note>original: *Wollust*; can refer to general vigor or sexual desire</note>. Dissolved in **water of life**, it strengthens the **memory**. If made into an **ointment** <note>original: *unguento*</note> with a little capon-fat <note>fat from a castrated rooster</note> and rubbed into the eyes, it creates clear vision.

## Monoceros or the
## Unicorn.

The horn of this animal, when burned and its salt extracted—as has been done with others—and well purified and clarified with **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritu vini*; high-proof alcohol used as a solvent</note>, then three grains dissolved and taken in an **extract of theriac** or **theriac-water** <term>theriac was a complex herbal "universal" remedy used as an antidote to poison and plague</term>, while being covered warmly and perspiring well thereafter, drives away the **pestilence**, the **quartan fever** <note>a fever recurring every four days, often associated with malaria</note>, and all **fevers**. It cleanses the foul blood that has been infected with poison; and if a person has ingested poison, let him take this remedy in this manner, and it shall not harm him. It also dispels **melancholy thoughts**, strengthens the brain, produces a good memory, and rouses the heart to gentleness and joy. It is also used in this way to great effect for the **bloody flux** <note>original: *rohten Ruhr*; dysentery</note> and whatever causes intestinal **ruptures** <note>original: *Durchbruch*; severe purging or internal lesions</note>.

## Capra, the Goat.

One **Quentchen** <term>an old unit of weight, approximately 3.6 grams</term> of this salt, taken with two or three spoonfuls of the goat’s own milk, drives away **rheum of the eyes** <note>discharges or watering of the eye</note> and makes them clear and bright, and stills **catarrhs of the head**. This salt, mixed with honey and applied as a plaster, cools and heals **carbuncles** <note>painful, pus-filled boils</note> and all hot and burning sores. Teeth rubbed with goat-salt are made white, and it settles swollen, high, and inflamed gums. Taken with its milk, as mentioned before, it stills **stitches in the side** <note>pleurisy or sharp abdominal pain</note> and also expels worms from the human body. When mixed in **equal parts** <note>original: *ana*; a common medical abbreviation for equal quantities</note> with burnt **saltpeter** <note>potassium nitrate</note>, dissolved in **endive-water**, and used to gargle the throat, it drives away **scurvy** <note>original: *Scharbeock*</note> and **mouth rot** <note>original: *Mundfäule*; inflammatory conditions of the mouth or gums</note>.

## Cervus, the Deer or Hart.

This salt, with one **Quentchen** <term>an old unit of weight, approximately 3.6 grams</term> dissolved in vinegar, to which a few crushed juniper berries and half a **Lot** <term>approx. 15-16 grams</term> of finely chopped **Bertram** <note>original: *Bertram*; the plant Pellitory of Spain, known for its pungent root that causes salivation</note> have been added and boiled together—when held in the mouth several times as warm as one can bear it—takes away **toothache**, cleanses decaying teeth, and draws to itself all the phlegm and impurity from which such pain arises. It is also good when taken by those who **spit blood**, regulates the **menstrual cycle** <note>original: *Frauen Zeit*; "women's time"</note>, and dispels **jaundice** <note>original: *gelbe Sucht*; "the yellow sickness"</note>.

If one uses the salt extracted from burned **hartshorn** <note>deer antler</note> that was shed between the **two Lady Days** <note>The period between the Assumption (August 15) and the Nativity of Mary (September 8), traditionally considered a time of peak medicinal potency</note>, it is much better than others, and possesses the same power as the salt that might be made from the **Unicorn**.

### Porcus, the Pig or Swine.

One Quentchen mixed with sugar and nut oil and taken internally breaks the **stone in the bladder**.

### Sciurus, the Squirrel.

## Lupus, the Wolf.

## Talpa, the Mole.

# Fifth Part of the Last Testament

### Rana, the Frog.

Water distilled from frogs—or those of their kind—in which half a **Loth** <term>a historical unit of weight, approximately 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of salt has been dissolved into four **Loth** of the liquid, draws out all poison when cloths are soaked in it and placed upon the sores of the poisonous **plague buboes** <note>original: *Pestilenzbeulen*; the swollen lymph nodes characteristic of the bubonic plague</note>. It is also an excellent cooling agent. If held in the mouth for a time and constantly refreshed, it draws out all pus and phlegm from the ailment under the tongue called **"the frogs"** <note>original: *die Frösche*; known in medicine as a ranula, a mucus-filled cyst named for its resemblance to a frog's underbelly</note>. Used in warm wine for three consecutive days—taking a fourth part of a **Quentin** <term>a small weight, approximately 4 grams</term> each time—it takes away all fever arising from a **phlegmatic state** <note>original: *phlegmatischen Zustand*; referring to an imbalance of the "phlegm" humor in Galenic medicine</note>.

### Salt of Elk Hooves.

When the oil has first been drawn off from the **elk hooves** <note>original: *Elends-Klauen*; the hooves of the elk or moose were a famous historical remedy for epilepsy</note> through distillation, the residue should be burnt to powder in a sealed pot. From this, the fine salt is extracted, just as with other substances. This is a magnificent **medicine** <note>original: *medicamentum*</note> for the **falling sickness** <note>original: *hinfallenden Sucht*; a historical term for epilepsy</note> when three **grains** <term>the smallest unit of weight, roughly 0.06 grams</term> are taken with the **breath of life** <note>original: *aura vitæ*; likely referring to a specific spagyric or alchemical preparation intended to restore the vital spirits</note>. Furthermore, a half **Quentin** used with **peony-rose water** strengthens the heart and all limbs, drives away inflamed and poisonous blood, and brings a good, peaceful sleep.

### *Perdix*, the Partridge.

Taking nine or ten **grains** <term>the smallest unit of weight, roughly 0.06 grams</term> of this salt with a good **brandy** <note>original: *Brantwein*; distilled spirits used as a solvent or carrier</note> awakens the desire for the **marital act** <note>original: *ehlichen Wercke*; a polite historical reference to sexual intercourse</note>. ### *Gallina*, the Hen.

Taking half a **Loth** <term>a historical unit of weight, approximately 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of its salt in a previously unsalted chicken broth serves as a softening for **constipation** <note>original: *Verstopffung des Leibs*; literally "blockage of the body"</note> and is useful for **cholera** <note>in early medicine, this often referred to an excess of yellow bile and digestive upset rather than the modern bacterial infection</note>, for it consumes and carries away all evil moisture. # Fifth Part of the Last Testament

## *Pavo*, the Peacock.

Peacock-salt <note>original: *Pfauen-Saltz*</note> does not allow foul blood to take root; used daily in doses of three or four grains in wine, it alleviates **gout** <term>original: *Podagra*; traditionally referring to gout of the foot, but often used generally for joint pain</term> and consumes the humors in the head that bring harm to the eyes.

## *Pica*, the Magpie. <note>original: *Atzel*</note>

This salt, dissolved in distilled magpie-water and applied with cloths to inflamed injuries, heals them, as well as the marks and spots on the face; it drives away all red blemishes and all discomfort associated with them. Taken with **stroke-water** <note>original: *Schlagwasser*; a medicinal water used to treat "Schlag" or apoplexy/paralysis</note> or the **solution of pearls** <term>original: *solutio perlarum*; an alchemical preparation where pearls are dissolved in an acidic medium, believed to have restorative powers</term>, it restores lost speech and produces a good memory.

## The Salt of Eggshells.

All salt from eggshells is powerful and has this **power** <term>original: *virtutem*</term> and virtue when taken with its own water distilled from eggs: to **dissolve** <term>original: *resolviren*; the alchemical process of breaking down a solid into a liquid state</term>; therefore it is also useful for **gout** <term>original: *Podagra*</term> and the **stone** <note>referring to kidney or bladder stones</note>. It dispels the **coagulated** <term>original: *coagulirte*</term> phlegm that settles upon the chest, promotes easy urination, and breaks up the hard, coarse, and evil blood which has settled and deposited itself in the limbs and veins due to anger, terror, or other causes.

# From Friar Basilius Valentinus.

## *Carpio*, the Carp.

A small amount [of the salt] applied with the pressed juice of unripe grapes <term>original: *unzeitigen Weintrauben*; often used to make verjuice, a sour liquid used in medicine for its cooling and astringent properties</term> to old sores <note>original: *Schäden*; likely referring to chronic wounds or ulcers</note> cleanses them and makes them whole. With the **oil** <note>original: *oleo*</note> that is distilled from its fat, it drives away **consumption** <term>original: *Schwindsucht*; a historical term for a wasting disease, usually tuberculosis</term>.

## *Variola trutta*, the Trout.

Taken with wine daily in a dose of about six **grains** <term>a small unit of weight; approximately 0.06 grams</term>, it produces good blood, a cheerful spirit, and a healthy heart; it increases desire, brings rest and sleep, and releases one from cares.

## *Anguilla*, the Eel.

Eel-salt <note>original: *Ahlen-Saltz*</note> used in distilled water made from warm rye bread <note>distilling water through or from bread was a common method to create a gentle medicinal carrier</note>, eight grains daily, restores lost hearing and makes the heart eager.

## *Cancer*, the Crayfish. <note>original: *Krebs*; while it can mean crab, in this context of European freshwater medicine, it usually refers to the crayfish.</note>

One **dram** <term>original: *Quenten*; about 3.6 grams</term> of crayfish-salt taken with its own water, which has been distilled from it, cleanses the bladder, breaks up and expels the **stone** <note>kidney or bladder stones</note>, and removes all ulcers of the lungs; it is especially effective for kidney sores that pass through the male member <note>the urethra</note>, and it also drives away the cough. The salt made into an ointment with honey and spread [upon the skin] heals all **chaps** <note>original: *Schrunden*; painful cracks or fissures in the skin</note> on the hands and feet. Furthermore, when mixed with an equal amount of **saltpeter-salt** <note>original: *Salpeter-Saltz*</note> prepared with sulfur, and a dram of this is taken in sorrel water or common spring water, it is a certain remedy beyond all other **cooling powders** <note>original: *Pulverlöschung*; preparations used to "extinguish" internal heat or inflammation</note>.

# Fifth Part of the Last Testament

For a person whose natural seed <note>original: *Saime*; referring to semen</note> escapes and exits against their will <note>referring to involuntary seminal emission or "nocturnal emissions"</note>, let him take the salt of crayfish, likewise the salt of eggshells, snail-salt, and the salt made from acorns in equal amounts. Dissolve a fourth part of a **dram** <term>original: *Quente*; a historical unit of weight, roughly 3.6 grams</term> of this in the liquid or extract of **crayfish eyes** <term>original: *Krebsaugen*; these are not actually eyes, but small calcareous stones found in the stomachs of molting crayfish, highly prized in historical pharmacy as an absorbent and antacid</term>. Taken daily for one month, it returns the seed to its right, natural, and proper course.

### *Halec*, the Herring.

One **scruple** <term>original: *Scrupel*; a unit of weight equal to 1.3 grams</term> of the salt of the herring used daily in fennel water creates good sight and consumes the darkness of the eyes <note>likely referring to cataracts or clouded vision</note>. This salt, mixed with an equal amount of pounded sulfur to make an ointment with pig's lard and smeared upon the body, drives away all scabbiness <note>original: *Räudigkeit*; often referring to mange or similar itchy skin conditions</note> of the skin, and makes the skin mild, soft, and tender.

### *Cochleæ terrestres*, Snails.

Snail-salt creates a good memory and serves for bladder and kidney stones. When burnt to ashes with its little house <note>the snail shell</note> and made into a salt, it brings a peaceful disposition, is good for all hardening of the nerves, and dissolves **gout** <term>original: *Podagra*; specifically gout affecting the feet</term>, especially if its **spirit** <term>original: *spiritus*; in alchemy, the volatile essence or liquid distillate of a substance</term> is driven over <note>distilled</note>; as is to be understood regarding all salts when gout and the like are mentioned.

<meta>catchword: Use</meta>

## Now follows further the method of how one should extract the salt from all precious stones.

Take whichever stone you wish and grind it until it is inconceivably fine, and grind an equal amount of **sulfur** <term>original: *Schwefel*</term> into it; cement it <note>a process of heating a solid in a sealed container with another substance to effect a chemical change</note> for 6 hours while closed. Afterward, calcine it strongly in a **muffle** <term>original: *Muffel*; a semi-cylindrical ceramic chamber used in a furnace to protect the material from direct flame</term> within an **assay furnace** <term>original: *Probirofen*; a small furnace used by metallurgists and alchemists for testing ores</term> for two hours, stirring it constantly. Then, pour the material while it is still glowing hot into a good, sharp, distilled wine vinegar; pour the vinegar off carefully once it has settled well, and rinse the material or the powder thoroughly with common distilled water. Afterward, dry the powder, moisten it with rose water, and form small cakes out of it. Then pour a good **spirit of juniper** <term>original: *spiritum juniperi*</term> over it and let it digest for a long time until you have extracted the **essence** <note>original: *essentiam*; the refined "soul" or medicinal concentrated part of the substance</note> of everything. Filter this through a delicate **filter paper** <term>original: *Maculatur*; a coarse paper used for straining liquids</term> and draw off the spirit of juniper in **Mary’s bath** <term>original: *Balneo Mariæ*; a water bath used for gentle, indirect heating</term>; the essence will remain at the bottom, which is used for other purposes.

Whatever remains from the extraction, rinse it well; then pour the corrosive distilled honey-water over it and extract the **salt in the proper manner** <note>original: *sal debito more*</note>. Distill the water away from it and rinse the remaining salt well **with spirit of wine** <term>original: *cum spiritu vini*; concentrated alcohol</term> through the frequent repetition of distillation; in this way, you will have the salt clear and pure.

Thus, in this way, one can make and extract the salt from any stone. For this purpose, stones can be used that are not suitable for cutting <note>referring to gems with flaws that make them unsuitable for jewelry</note>, or the small pieces that fall away from stones that have been cut.

<summary>This page outlines the alchemical procedure for extracting medicinal "salts" and "essences" from gemstones through calcination, acid baths, and distillation. It emphasizes that even gemstone scraps from jewelers can be recycled for these potent chemical preparations.</summary>

### Uses.

## Ruby.

Half a grain of this salt dissolved in **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritu vini*; a high-proof distilled alcohol</note> and dropped into weak eyes makes for clear vision and strengthens the eyes mightily. Also, taken in a spoonful of **brandy** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*, literally "water of life"; a strong distilled spirit</note>, it strengthens the heart, brings joy, and grants a good memory.

## Emerald.

One grain of this salt, taken with spirit of wine or a spoonful of brandy, helps those who have been poisoned; if they then lie down and sweat, it makes lost hair grow back and brings new hair to the spot. It drives away **melancholy** <note>original: *melancholiam*; in this context, a state of deep depression or a chemical imbalance of the "black bile" humor</note> and the **falling sickness** <note>original: *hinfallende Sucht*; a historical term for epilepsy</note> when taken and used in this way for a third time.

## Diamond.

Half a grain taken in an **oil of the sun** <note>original: *oleo solis*; an alchemical preparation of gold</note> or two **drams** <term>original: *Quintlein*; a small unit of weight, roughly 3.6 grams</term> of **potable gold** <note>original: *auri potabilis*; a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold in a drinkable, liquid form</note> expels **leprosy** <note>original: *Aussatz*; used here generally for severe skin diseases</note> and madness in a person; it strengthens the heart, makes one joyful, and drives away melancholy; it chases away heavy thoughts and sadness, crushes stones in the bladder, and dissolves coagulated **gout** <term>original: *Podagra*; specifically gout affecting the foot</term>; it drives poison away from the heart and creates good blood.

## Sapphire.

One grain of its salt dissolved in two drams of **potable silver** <note>original: *Luna potabili*; a medicinal tincture made from silver, associated with the moon</note> makes a person joyful, refreshes the spirit, strengthens the limbs, and consumes all evil **phlegmatic humors** <note>original: *phlegmatische Feuchtigkeiten*; according to ancient medicine, an excess of the "phlegm" humor caused sluggishness and respiratory issues</note>.

### Turquoise.

One grain of this salt taken, mixed with two grains of the **essence of Venus** <note>original: *essentia veneris*; an alchemical preparation of copper, which was associated with the planet Venus</note> and dissolved beforehand in a spoonful or two of **brandy** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*, literally "water of life"; a strong distilled spirit</note>, drives away **head-fluxes** <note>original: *Hauptflüsse*; a historical term for excess fluid or catarrh draining from the brain</note>, makes for a good, sharp eyesight, increases the seed in man and woman, and brings a particular appetite, desire, and arousal for carnal and human lust.

### Topaz.

One grain of this salt used in syrup of violets calms unnatural heat in the human body, stanches the bleeding of wounds and the nose, drives away unchastity, and consumes all **superfluity** <note>excessive or imbalanced bodily humors</note> that gives cause for it.

### Hyacinth.

Two grains of this salt taken with a little **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritu vini*; high-proof distilled alcohol</note> expels poison and all diseases caused by sorcery; it promotes the flow of urine and breaks up **potions** <note>original: *philtra*; usually referring to love potions or magical drafts intended to manipulate the recipient</note> if a person has eaten or drunk something evil. It makes the heart joyful, strengthens human power, grants a good memory, and protects against insanity; it keeps the lungs from all decay and heals **consumption** <note>original: *Schwindsucht*; a historical term for wasting diseases like tuberculosis</note>.

## Garnet, Carnelian, Amethyst, and Bloodstone.

These four stones have the same power and virtue. The weight of their salt is three grains, taken in the distilled water of **bloodroot** <note>original: *Blutkraut-Wurzel*; likely *Potentilla erecta* or *Sanguinaria*, plants historically used to stop bleeding</note>; it stanches the blood of wounds and the nose and brings cooling.

It dries out the evil moisture...

# Pearls.

AS **pearls** are softer and not subject to such hard coagulation <note>solidification or hardening</note> as other precious stones, so too must their salt be made by a much different **method** <note>original: *Methodum*</note> than was mentioned for the previous hard stones; its preparation, however, is as follows:

Take **pearls** and pour a sharp distilled **vinegar** upon them, and resolve the pearls as long as they will resolve, just as one is otherwise accustomed to making the **solution of pearls** <note>original: *solutio perlarum*</note>. Draw off the vinegar in a **Marie-bath** <note>original: *Balneo Mariæ*; a gentle water bath</note>; thus the pearl-powder remains at the bottom <note>original: *in fundo*</note>. Sweeten this well with spirit of wine until the sourness <note>original: *acerofitas*</note> is entirely gone from it and no more vinegar can be tasted in the powder, but it is quite pleasant on the tongue.

When that is done, put it afterward into a small glass flask and pour a good distilled **oil of cloves** <note>original: *Nägelein-Oel* or *oleum caryophyllorum*</note> upon it. Place it, sealed, into the Marie-bath and digest it for one month; then the true **essence** <note>original: *essentia*</note> of the pearls passes beautifully, clearly, and subtly into the oil of cloves. Pour this off carefully.

The **dregs** <note>original: *fæces*</note> that remain behind, reverberate <note>to heat in a furnace with air and flame</note> very subtly under a **muffle** <note>original: *Muffel*; a ceramic chamber in a furnace that protects the material from direct flame</note>, stirring constantly, for no longer than a quarter of an hour, so that the oil is burned and smoked away from it. When that is also accomplished, pour a good spirit of wine upon it and extract its salt by steady heat, and clarify it; thus you have the **salt of pearls** <note>original: *sal margaritarum*</note>.

Finally, as a farewell <note>original: *valete*; a Latin closing salutation</note>, I wish to reveal this secret of the neglected lime and first show how its spirit is driven out of it. Take unslaked lime <note>original: *ungelöschten Kalck*; quicklime or calcium oxide, which reacts violently with water</note>, as much as you wish, crush and rub it on a very dry stone into a subtle powder. Then take such prepared lime out of the **flask** <term>Kolben: a glass vessel used for distillation or digestion</term>, rub it small, and add to it a tenth part of **salt of tartar** <term>salis tartari: potassium carbonate, usually derived from the sediment of wine barrels</term> that is beautifully pure and has no more **dregs** <note>original: *feces*; the solid impurities or sediment</note>.

Mix and rub it all well together and place it in a well-coated **retort** <term>retort: a glass vessel with a long, downward-curving neck used for dry distillation</term>, filling it only to one third. Attach a large **flask**, very well **luted** and secured; but note that the **flask** where the neck of the **retort** is inserted must have a small tube about the width of a finger, to which one must [attach] another **flask** containing a little **spirit of wine**...

## Jodocus von Rehe’s Particular and Universal Process.
<note>In alchemy, a "Particular" process aims to transform specific metals, while a "Universal" process seeks the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

One prepares a silver as pure as can ever be made; this is dissolved <note>original: "solviret."</note> in our *spirit of Mercury* <note>original: "spiritu Mercurii."</note> into a thick, sticky water. The spirit of mercury is then distilled off, so that the *Luna* <note>The alchemical name for Silver, associated with the moon.</note> remains at the bottom in a beautiful blue and white color. This is reduced *through digestion* <note>original: "per digestionem," referring to the application of gentle, continuous heat.</note> into a dry, dusty powder. Into this, one *imbibes* <note>original: "imbibirt"; to saturate a dry substance with liquid.</note> or lets fall drop by drop our *animal sulfur* <note>original: "sulphur animale."</note>, which lies hidden in the center of our Mercury. It is allowed to *macerate* <note>original: "maceriren"; to soften or soak.</note> together in a *circulation glass* <note>original: "circulir-Glas"; a vessel designed so that evaporating vapors condense and flow back down, "circulating" the matter.</note>. And when the *silver-calx* <note>original: "Silberkalck"; the powdery residue left after a metal is dissolved or burned.</note> will accept no more, one saturates it and *fixes* <note>original: "figiret"; the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note> it until all moisture and vapor disappear, which can happen in five weeks. Then, one melts it with a little *borax* <note>original: "borras," a flux used to help metals melt and flow.</note> into a *body* <note>original: "corpus"; a solid metallic mass.</note>

# Writings of Basilius Valentinus.

## The Practice of the work, as it was recorded in the mentioned book.

The Practice of the true Philosopher's Stone, I have recorded—in the same form as it stood in the mentioned Doctor’s secret little book, for fear of potential forgetfulness—in the following protocol in the city of Hormoborn in the Bishopric of Paderborn in the year of Christ 1604, on the 11th of August. Take <note>original "℞", the traditional apothecary symbol for 'recipe' or 'take'</note> 10 lbs of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>Sulfate minerals; alchemists often used "Oil of Vitriol" (sulfuric acid) as a primary solvent.</note> (understand, one must purify the vitriol as highly as is mentioned at the start of the following Practice, and the secret *spirit* <note>original: "spiritum"</note> made from it). Put it into a <term>retort</term> <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-curving neck used for distilling liquids.</note> and a receiver <note>original: "Vorlage"</note> for it, well-sealed <note>original: "verlutiret"; sealed with 'lute,' a tough paste used to make joints airtight</note>. Wall it up well in a furnace that is wide, so that the coals which one pours into the top of the furnace can fall down beside the retort. Drive out the *spirits* <note>original: "spiritus"</note> slowly at first for four hours; after that, one must continue for half an hour with the greatest possible fire. And when you find that the red corrosive *oil* <note>original: "oleum"</note> begins to come, then let it cool, and cast away the remaining *matter* <note>original: "materiam"</note>, for it is no longer useful, unless one wished to use it in other ways. ### Of the Green and Red Lions.

The Green Lion of *Theophrastus* <note>referring to the famous alchemist Paracelsus</note> caused me much trouble before I learned to recognize it; but when I learned to recognize the Green Lion <note>often a symbol for acidic solvents or raw vitriol</note>, the Red Lion <note>a symbol for the final, perfected Stone</note> also appeared quite proudly, and one proceeds from the other. To such knowledge no man can easily come, unless God sends him a faithful master—as I, *Jodocus von Rehe*, can well sing a little song about <note>an idiom meaning he speaks from hard-won experience</note>.

# On the Preparation of Precious Stones through the Spirit of Mercury.

In our Mercurial water or spirit, one finds the color of the diamond; in the body of Gold <note>original: "corpore Solis"; the sun is the alchemical symbol for gold</note>, the carbuncle stone <note>a deep red gemstone, often a garnet or ruby</note>; in Iron <note>original: "Marte"; Mars is the symbol for iron</note>, that of rubies; in Copper <note>original: "Venere"; Venus is the symbol for copper</note>, that of emeralds; in Lead <note>original: "Saturno"; Saturn is the symbol for lead</note>, that of garnets; in Tin <note>original: "Jove"; Jupiter is the symbol for tin</note>, that of topaz; in Mercury, that of crystal; and in Silver <note>original: "Luna"; the moon is the symbol for silver</note>, that of sapphire.

### Practical Procedure for this Work.

If one wishes to make these precious stones, the soul of the metals <note>the "soul" refers to the concentrated color or essence extracted from a metal</note> must be extracted with the spirit of mercury, and this soul must then be brought through <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the alchemical process of decay or fermentation used to break down a substance</note> first into a mass, and then into a fatty powder. 

Then, one takes fine Venetian glass <note>highly prized for its clarity</note> or crystals, ground as subtly as possible and dusted through a small silk cloth, washed clean, and dried again. A portion of this is placed into a melting crucible and allowed to melt thoroughly in a strong melting-fire. Then, whichever of these extraction-tinctures <note>the metallic essences mentioned above</note> one desires is thrown upon it. This quickly brings the glass into flux and colors it with whatever colors one wishes to have. Afterward, it is poured out into molds—small or large, round or angular, as one desires. 

However, they are still dark and not transparent; therefore, one must glow them <note>heat them until they are red-hot</note> held within a pair of tongs, and quench them in our spirit of Mercury. Thus they become transparent and shining; this I have tested by experiment.

# A very useful specific procedure <note>original: "particular"; in alchemy, a "particular" is a recipe that transmutes a specific amount of base metal into gold or silver, rather than the "universal" medicine which acts on all things</note>, which I, Jodocus von Rehe, have performed many times and from which I have had good profit and surplus; with one drachm <note>original: "Quintlein"; roughly 3.7 grams</note> of the same, two ounces <note>original: "Loht"; a historical German unit of weight</note> of silver <note>original: "Lunae"; the Moon is the alchemical symbol for silver</note> are tinted into good gold.

Take gold that has been cast through antimony <note>a process used to purify gold to its highest degree</note>, melt it once more, cast it into a bar, laminate it <note>beat it into thin, paper-like sheets</note>, and in a vial pour good spirit of salt <note>hydrochloric acid</note> over it, two fingers high. Seal the vial at the top and keep it in warm ashes until the spirit of salt is colored a beautiful yellow. Pour that off and add more, letting it color itself again in the warmth; do this until all the gold is dissolved. 

Afterward, draw off all the solutions in a small flask until dry, so that the gold calx <note>a fine powder produced by the chemical breakdown of the metal</note> is left behind like blood. Wash this clean with warm distilled water so that the saltiness and all sharpness is removed. Dry the gold calx, which is as beautiful as a ruby. Weigh the gold calx and pour three times as much of our secret spirit of Mercury over it. Seal the small glass and set it in warm ashes; thus the spirit of Mercury draws the soul <note>the "anima" or the essential color and life-force of the metal</note> out of the gold calx into itself and turns completely golden-yellow, like a hyacinth <note>a reddish-orange gemstone, likely a zircon</note>. 

The body of the sun <note>original: "corpus solis"; the physical remains of the gold</note> remains lying at the bottom, whitish like silver, for it has been robbed of its soul. Pour the colored spirit of Mercury off from the body of the sun into a clean flask, place a distillation head <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of a still</note> upon it, and attach a receiver, well-sealed with luting <note>an airtight clay or paste seal</note>. Begin to distill gently, and the spirit of Mercury will pass over quite volatilely along with the soul of the Sun. They have united with one another in such a way that they can no longer be separated. Repeat this distillation twice.

Then take pure steel filings and extract from them their *soul* <note>original: "animam"; in alchemy, the "soul" refers to the essential oily or sulfurous principle of a metal</note>, in the manner I will instruct you at the end of this process. 

Once you have the *soul of iron* <note>original: "animam martis"; Mars is the alchemical name for iron</note>, weigh it and place it in a glass, and pour three times as much of our *spirit of mercury* <note>original: "spiritus Mercurii"</note> over it. Place it in mild ashes <note>to provide gentle, indirect heat</note>, and the *spirit of mercury* will also bring it into the *first matter* <note>original: "primam materiam"; the base, chaotic state of matter required for alchemical transformation</note>, just as happened with the gold, and it will become a blood-red *liquid* <note>original: "liquor"</note>. Pour it into a small flask and attach a *receiver* <note>original: "recipienten"; a vessel used to collect the results of distillation</note> to it, and distill it first gently, then more strongly; in this way, the *spirit of mercury* and the *soul of iron* will rise over together and become united with one another. 

Repeat the *distillation* a second time, and it will become even more volatile and can no longer be separated from the *spirit of mercury*. When you have this beautiful red *liquid*, you have a perfect *medicine* to heal *dysentery* <note>original: "dysenteriam"</note> and all "breakthroughs" <note>likely referring to various types of flux or chronic discharges</note> of the human body, as well as other ailments that are subject to *martial jurisdiction* <note>illnesses traditionally associated with the planet Mars, such as fevers, inflammations, or blood disorders</note>. When you have brought this so far, you have won, for you have a *medicine* with which you can *cure all human bodies*. 

However, if you wish to use it for metallic *transmutation*, take your volatilized *oil of gold* <note>original: "Goldöhl"</note> which has united with the *spirit of mercury*, and likewise the *soul of iron*. Pour these two souls together into a small flask, seal a *distilling head* <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of a still, shaped like a helmet</note> onto it, and attach a *receiver*; draw them over together in the ashes. The result is yellow; if one places this *liquid* in the sun, it gives off more than a hundred kinds of beautiful yellow flowing streaks, so that it may rightly be held as a wonder—

<summary>This page describes the laboratory process for creating a combined "spirit" of gold and iron. The resulting liquid is presented as both a powerful medicinal panacea for "martial" illnesses and a key ingredient for the alchemical transmutation of metals.</summary>
<keywords>drinkable gold, soul of iron, spirit of mercury, distillation, dysentery, martial jurisdiction, transmutation, oil of gold</keywords>

[to] be [looked upon], and they delight the eyes; and thus both the souls and the *spirit of mercury* <note>original: "spiritus mercurii"</note> have united and bound themselves together in such a way that they can never be separated for all eternity. Now it is necessary that one also gives and assigns a metallic *body* <note>original: "corpus"</note> to this united metallic *liquid* <note>original: "liquor"</note> or oil; for this *liquid* cannot become a *body* on its own, even if it were to stand in the fire forever, for they are pure souls and spirits, and have left their *body* and separated themselves from it. For the soul of the gold has separated from its body, just as the *soul of iron* <note>original: "anima martis"</note> has also left its *body* and united with the *soul of the Sun* <note>original: "anima Solis"; the alchemical soul of gold</note>. Likewise, the *spirit of mercury* has also separated from its *sulfur* <note>original: "sulphure"</note> and *salt* <note>original: "sale"</note> and entered into a heavenly substance, just as it has united and bound itself with the two souls. 

Therefore, weigh out one *lot* <note>a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15-17 grams</note> of your *liquid*, and take eight *lots* of fine *calx of silver* <note>original: "Silberkalck"; silver reduced to a powder through heat or acid</note>; reverberate it <note>heat it in a furnace where the flames are "reverberated" or bent back onto the material</note> for two hours under a *muffle* <note>a clay semi-cylinder that protects the material from direct contact with fuel/flames</note> very gently, so that it becomes dry and thirsty. When this has been done, put it into the vial and pour the *liquid* over it; it will then soak it up like leather absorbs oil. Then let it dry and *coagulate* <note>solidify or thicken</note> it; test it on a glowing metal plate. If it still smokes, it must be fully *fixed* <note>original: "figirt"; rendered stable so it no longer evaporates when heated</note>; once it is fixed, *reduce* <note>original: "reducirs"; the process of smelting a metallic powder back into solid metal</note> it with *borax* <note>original: "borras"</note>.

[...so] filter the solution while warm through filter paper <note>original: "Maculatur"; specifically waste or blotting paper used for filtration</note> and let it gently evaporate <note>original: "evaporiren"</note> until a film <note>original: "Häutlein"; a pellicle forming on the surface, indicating the liquid is saturated</note> forms. ### Calcination of Silver <note>original: "Calcinatio Lunæ"; "Luna" is the alchemical name for silver</note>.

Some of it is cemented <note>original: "cementirt"; a process of heating metal in a dry powder to alter its properties</note> with common salt and quicklime so that it becomes brittle, so that it can be rubbed into a powder, which draws out the blackness <note>impurities or the "sulfurous" part</note> of the silver.

->*Otherwise:*<-

Silver is also dissolved in nitric acid <note>original: "Aqua fort" or Aqua Fortis</note>; the nitric acid is drawn off <note>removed by distillation</note>, it is washed <note>original: "edulcoriret"</note>, then dissolved with spirit of vitriol <note>sulfuric acid</note> or spirit of mercury, and distilled from it; which spirit of mercury is always good.

### Lute of Wisdom <note>original: "Lutum sapientiæ"; a specialized airtight sealant used to close alchemical vessels</note>.

Take one part of quicklime <note>original: "calcis vivæ"</note>, two parts of cinnabar <note>original: "cinabrii"; mercury sulfide</note>, and one part of common salt <note>original: "salis communis"</note>, mixed with egg white.

Though he made leaps and labored <note>original: "laboriret"; referring to performing alchemical experiments</note> now in **Spain**, then in **Westphalia**, then in **Alsace**, it is indeed true that it sounds somewhat strange. However, it may well be that he traveled after the Spanish mines, as their <term>mercury ore<note>original: "minera mercurii"</note></term> and some other <term>minerals<note>original: "mineralia"</note></term> far exceed many others in quality. On his return, he went to **Holland** and further into the **Paderborn** region, undertaking some <term>labors<note>original: "labores"; alchemical operations</note></term> at each place, but finally resolved to remain in **Alsace**, as it is an exceedingly noble land. But let that be as it may, little depends on it, provided that something good may be learned from his <term>procedures<note>original: "Processen"</note></term>, as they indeed seem to proceed from a good <term>foundation<note>original: "fundament"</note></term>, since they agree very well with the writings of **Basilius**.

As for what else concerns the writings of **Basilius Valentinus**, it should be remembered that if one or another bookseller, who has dealt with such **Basilian** writings until now and wishes to have them printed again after the current copies <note>original: "Exemplarien"</note> are sold, they might report this to us beforehand without trouble. We would be prepared, as much as possible for us, to help bring such writings back into their proper order, and further to make diligent inquiry as to whether more <term>manuscripts<note>original: "manuscripta"</note></term> by him are to be had which have not yet been printed. For a friend wished to assure us that a large manuscript of many pages of **Basilius Valentinus’s** matters is still in existence; however, we have not yet been able to see it, much less take part in it. We shall, however, spare no further diligence in inquiring after these and similar useful writings, and what is obtained shall be shared for the <term>public good<note>original: "Bono publico"</note></term>; with which, for 
->this time, we all recommend ourselves to Divine grace and<-
->protection.<-
